The footwear retailer opened 21 stores and closed nine during the quarter. As of September 30, 2026, its retail network comprised 1,053 stores across 223 cities in 31 states and Union Territories. Metro Brands operates a portfolio that includes Metro Shoes, Mochi, Walkway, MetroActiv, Da Vinchi and J. Fontini, alongside international footwear brands such as Crocs, Clarks, Skechers and Puma. Its product range also includes accessories such as handbags, belts and wallets.
The company's Q2 FY27 performance reflects continued revenue and earnings growth, alongside ongoing store network expansion and a growing contribution from digital sales. With a larger share of festive demand expected in the next quarter, the company will enter the upcoming period with a focus on retail operations, brand development, and omnichannel sales.
Thermocool Home Appliances Ltd plans to invest approximately Rs 40 crore in a new manufacturing facility in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, to increase production capacity and strengthen its in-house manufacturing operations. The proposed facility will manufacture air coolers, fans, and small appliances as the company expands its presence in India's home appliances market.
The facility will cover approximately two acres, with a built-up area of around 40,000 to 60,000 sq ft. Its planned annual production capacity will be around 3 to 4 lakh air coolers, 3 to 5 lakh fans and 1 to 2 lakh small appliances. The investment is aimed at increasing manufacturing capacity, improving backward integration and giving the company greater control over production, product quality and supply chain operations. The expansion is also expected to support Thermocool's efforts to meet consumer demand across key markets.
Tushar Gupta, Director of Operations, Thermocool Home Appliances Ltd said, “The proposed manufacturing facility is an important step in strengthening our production capabilities and supporting our long-term growth plans. We are focusing on greater backward integration and building a manufacturing ecosystem that allows us to respond more efficiently to changing consumer demand. The facility will also support our efforts to expand our product portfolio and strengthen our presence across key markets.”
Thermocool currently operates a 25,000 sq ft manufacturing plant in Ghaziabad and is working to increase its production capabilities. The company currently manufactures approximately 2,000 to 3,000 air coolers per day and plans to increase daily output by around 25 percent to 35 percent. The planned expansion will incorporate semi-automation, AI-based quality control, and sustainable manufacturing practices. These measures are intended to improve production efficiency and quality management as the company scales its operations.
Thermocool has more than 200 stock-keeping units (SKUs) across large and small appliance categories, with air coolers remaining a key product segment. The company has also achieved around 90 percent backward integration in air-cooler manufacturing, enabling it to exercise greater control over the production process.
Tanuj Gupta, Director of Sales, Thermocool Home Appliances Ltd said, “The home appliances market is evolving rapidly, with consumers looking for products that offer performance, value and reliability. Our manufacturing expansion will help us respond to these changing requirements while strengthening our distribution and market presence. We are also exploring opportunities in new categories as we continue to expand our portfolio.”
Alongside its manufacturing expansion, Thermocool is working to increase its distribution reach across India. The company currently has more than 300 distributors and a presence in approximately 5,000 retail stores. It is also expanding its visibility across e-commerce and digital commerce platforms.
The company is evaluating opportunities to enter the air-conditioner segment and is exploring other categories, including washing machines, refrigerators and televisions. The proposed Ghaziabad facility is expected to support its broader product expansion plans and strengthen its domestic manufacturing capabilities. The investment comes as Thermocool looks to increase production, develop its distribution network and expand its presence across India's home appliances market. The proposed facility will add to its existing manufacturing operations and support its plans to enter new product categories.
Zepto has partnered with ITC to introduce Dazzle Vibe Matches: LIT Parivar Edition, a limited-edition matchbox collection inspired by Indian family dynamics and Diwali celebrations. The collection will be available on Zepto across select markets from October 21, 2026. The collaboration brings a collectible format to an everyday household product, drawing on the traditional appeal of matchbox designs.
The collection features themes centred on family relationships, festive gatherings and the interactions that shape Diwali celebrations. The initiative also marks Zepto's first exclusive collectible developed in collaboration with a brand. Through the limited-edition release, the quick commerce platform is exploring a new format for brand collaborations, combining festive products with the appeal of collecting distinctive designs.
Chandan Mendiratta, Chief Brand Officer, Zepto said, “Dazzle Vibe Matches: LIT Parivar Edition marks Zepto’s first foray into collectibles through a special collaboration with ITC. We’re bringing back the nostalgia of matchbox collecting with a limited-edition design inspired by the fun, drama, and togetherness of the festive season. This is the first of many unique drops that are planned for our users, with more exciting collaborations to look forward to on Zepto. We thank ITC and our sellers for enabling this.”
Rohit Dogra, Chief Executive, Matches and Agarbatti Business Division, ITC Ltd added, “Through our collaboration with Zepto, we’re bringing a fresh perspective to the nostalgia of matchbox collecting with Dazzle Vibe Matches: LIT Parivar Edition. Inspired by the vibrant dynamics of Indian families and the spirit of Diwali, this limited-edition collection reimagines a familiar everyday object as a collectible. It’s a special way to celebrate the little things that bring people together while introducing a new generation to the charm of collecting.”
The collection will be available on Zepto from October 21, 2026, in select markets. The company plans to introduce more collectible releases through future collaborations, giving users access to additional limited-edition products on its platform.
The partnership highlights how quick commerce platforms and consumer goods companies are exploring new product formats and brand collaborations during major shopping occasions such as Diwali. For Zepto, the initiative also creates an opportunity to introduce exclusive products alongside its regular assortment of household essentials and festive merchandise.
Home services platform Urban Company is exploring a fresh fundraising plan just over a year after its stock market debut in September 2025. The proposed capital raise comes as the company continues to invest in its instant household services business, InstaHelp, amid rising competition in the segment.
In an exchange filing, Urban Company said its board will meet on October 16 to consider raising funds through equity shares or securities convertible into equity shares, in one or more tranches. The company is evaluating multiple routes, including preferential allotment, private placement, a qualified institutional placement (QIP), or any other legally permissible method, either individually or in combination.
The company is also scheduled to announce its second-quarter results for FY27 on the same day.
The fundraising proposal comes as spending on InstaHelp continues to affect Urban Company's financial performance. The vertical is facing competition from players such as Snabbit and Pronto, while its expansion has added pressure to profitability.
Urban Company reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 235 crore in FY26, compared with a net profit of Rs 240 crore in FY25. However, operating revenue increased 34 percent year-on-year to Rs 1,692 crore.
In Q1 FY27, operating revenue grew 44 percent year-on-year to Rs 528 crore. The company's consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 65 crore from Rs 98 crore in the preceding quarter. Excluding InstaHelp, Urban Company recorded an adjusted EBITDA profit of Rs 67 crore.
InstaHelp's revenue increased 26 percent quarter-on-quarter to approximately Rs 11 crore. However, its adjusted EBITDA loss widened to Rs 132 crore from Rs 119 crore in Q4 FY26. On a per-order basis, the adjusted EBITDA loss improved to Rs 346 from Rs 447 during the same period.
During the Q1 FY27 earnings call, co-founder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal indicated that investment in InstaHelp would remain elevated as the company works to strengthen its position in the category. He said the business would require investment for at least the next two years.
Management also expects InstaHelp to operate with lower margins than Urban Company's core consumer services business in India. The company is working towards achieving break-even in the vertical by FY31 and does not expect it to generate profits over the next five years.
The proposed fundraise comes amid a broader trend of listed technology companies returning to capital markets after their IPOs. Several new-age businesses have pursued QIPs and other equity fundraising routes to finance expansion and strengthen their balance sheets.
Kissht parent OnEMI Technology Solutions received shareholder approval to raise up to Rs 832 crore through a preferential issue, around four months after raising approximately Rs 926 crore through its IPO. Swiggy raised Rs 10,000 crore through a QIP in December 2025, about a year after its market debut. Ola Electric raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June 2026, while Ather Energy secured Rs 1,300 crore through a QIP approximately 14 months after its IPO.
Other companies, including Zaggle, RateGain and Nazara, have also raised capital through QIPs. Travel technology company ixigo raised approximately $146 million through a preferential issue around 16 months after its listing.
Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed Rs 1,000 crore initial public offering (IPO). The public issue will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 500 crore by existing shareholders.
As part of the OFS, Brainbees Solutions, the parent company of FirstCry, will sell shares worth Rs 300 crore, while Anadya Bon Merchari LLP plans to offload shares valued at Rs 200 crore. Swara Baby Products submitted its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) to SEBI in July this year.
The company intends to allocate Rs 198.2 crore from the fresh issue proceeds towards establishing a new manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh. Another Rs 100 crore is earmarked for the repayment of certain borrowings. Additionally, Rs 27.5 crore will be invested in its subsidiaries, Solis Hygiene, Swara Hygiene and KAEHPL, to repay debt. The remaining funds will be directed towards acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
Swara Baby Products may also explore a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 100 crore in consultation with its book-running lead managers. Any amount raised through such a placement would be adjusted against the fresh issue, subject to the applicable terms.
Established in 2018, Swara Baby Products manufactures a range of disposable hygiene products, including baby diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins and panty liners. Brainbees Solutions, its corporate promoter, is also among its key customers, alongside Piramal Pharma and Himalaya Wellness.
The company reported an increase in operating revenue of 23 percent to Rs 1,163.9 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 942.97 crore in FY25. Its profit rose 18 percent to Rs 95.58 crore during the same period. EBITDA increased to Rs 192.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 162.72 crore in the previous fiscal year.
B2B e-commerce platform Udaan returned to revenue growth in FY26 after reporting a decline in the previous fiscal year, with its gross merchandise value (GMV) increasing 12.6 percent year-on-year to Rs 5,134 crore from Rs 4,561 crore in FY25. The Bengaluru-based company also reduced its net loss by 19.2 percent to Rs 852 crore.
Founded in 2016 by former Flipkart executives Vaibhav Gupta, Sujeet Kumar and Amod Malviya, Udaan connects brands, wholesalers and retailers through its B2B e-commerce platform. Its business generates revenue through goods sales, logistics, platform fees, credit services and advertising.
Udaan recorded a GMV of approximately Rs 10,000 crore in FY22. Its subsequent decline reflected a strategic shift away from non-core categories such as lifestyle and general merchandise towards groceries and essential goods.
During FY26, material expenses increased 11.3 percent to Rs 4,859 crore from Rs 4,367 crore in the previous fiscal year. Finance costs rose 33.5 percent to Rs 247 crore, while logistics expenses increased 16.7 percent to Rs 182 crore.
Revenue growth and lower ESOP costs contributed to the reduction in net losses, extending Udaan’s annual loss-reduction trend to four consecutive years. Its net loss stood at Rs 2,075 crore in FY23 and Rs 1,674.1 crore in FY24 before declining to Rs 1,055 crore in FY25.
Udaan has also pursued acquisitions and financing initiatives to strengthen its distribution network and financial position. In September 2026, the company agreed to acquire Swiggy’s retail distribution business, Lynk Logistics, for Rs 500 crore. Under the proposed transaction, Swiggy will receive an approximately 2.8 percent stake in Udaan through preference shares and invest an additional Rs 75 crore for a 0.4 percent stake. The deal is expected to add Lynk’s brand partnerships and retail network to Udaan’s distribution operations.
In March 2026, Udaan’s parent company, Trustroot, acquired Info Edge’s entire 26.14 percent stake in Shopkirana for $32.97 million. In exchange, Info Edge received preference shares representing a 2.02 percent stake in Trustroot and committed an additional $1.72 million, taking its fully diluted shareholding in the company to 2.13 percent.
Udaan has also announced a structured financing transaction worth approximately $160 million to strengthen its balance sheet and simplify its capital structure ahead of its long-term public market plans.
The company is preparing for a potential initial public offering (IPO) and is reportedly targeting profitability by the end of 2027 or the first quarter of 2028.
Amazon Retail, which operates Amazon Now and Amazon Fresh in India, reported a nearly 50 percent increase in revenue from operations to Rs 3,065 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 2,051 crore in FY25. However, its net loss more than tripled to Rs 1,158 crore as expenses grew faster than revenue.
The company earned an additional Rs 15 crore in other income, taking its total revenue to Rs 3,080 crore during the fiscal year. Its operating income primarily comes from the sale of goods through Amazon Now and Amazon Fresh.
Despite the growth in revenue, Amazon Retail's total expenses surged 71.8 percent year-on-year to Rs 4,239 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,468 crore in FY25. Material procurement accounted for approximately 68 percent of total expenses, while delivery charges stood at Rs 529 crore. The company also incurred Rs 248 crore in platform fees and Rs 442 crore in legal expenses.
The rising cost base affected profitability, leaving Amazon Retail with a gross margin of around 5.08 percent. Its EBITDA stood at negative Rs 1,136 crore, while its EBITDA margin and return on capital employed (ROCE) declined to -37.06 percent and -235.22 percent, respectively. On a unit economics basis, the company spent approximately Rs 1.38 for every rupee earned in revenue.
The financial performance comes as Amazon increases its investments in India's quick commerce market, where Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto remain major competitors. Amazon plans to invest $3 billion in its Indian quick commerce business by 2030, including around $1 billion by the end of 2027 and another $2 billion through 2030.
Amazon said its quick commerce business crossed $1 billion in annualised gross sales over the preceding three months, describing it as the fastest-growing e-commerce business within its India operations.
Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto collectively account for 77 percent of the quick commerce market, while Amazon holds a 6.2 percent share. The company currently operates approximately 750 quick commerce stores and aims to increase this number to around 1,300 by April 2027.
Amazon's expansion highlights the investment required to compete in India's quick commerce sector. Sustaining growth will depend on increasing order volumes, improving fulfilment efficiency, and controlling operating costs. Converting higher revenue into sustainable profitability remains a key challenge as the company expands its presence in the market.
Bla Bli Blu, a Gurugram-based fragrance startup, has achieved an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 250 crore and turned EBITDA-positive within roughly a year of its launch. The development marks a financial milestone for the company as it expands its presence in India's fragrance market. Founded in July 2025 by Rajat Khullar, Durgesh Agarwal and Kushal Aggarwal, Bla Bli Blu had reported an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 100 crore six months ago, according to a company statement.
Its latest milestone reflects an increase in its revenue run rate as the business scales its sales and distribution channels. The company entered the Indian fragrance market to address the gap between mass-market perfumes and premium international fragrance labels. Its business strategy focuses on providing consumers with alternatives across these segments.
Bla Bli Blu's growth has been supported by a combination of e-commerce and quick-commerce channels. While online marketplaces provide access to consumers across a wider geography, quick-commerce platforms offer another route for product discovery and purchasing. The company has also developed revenue streams and established marketing and distribution partnerships to support its expansion.
Rajat Khullar, Founder said, "Our team has built revenue streams and lined up marketing and channel partners to bring this vision to fruition. Becoming EBITDA-positive is a moment of great pride for us, and shows the strength of our distinctive approach to marketing, sales, and business growth."
The company's move into positive EBITDA indicates that its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation have turned positive. However, this measure does not necessarily mean the business is profitable after accounting for all expenses, including interest, taxes and depreciation. Bla Bli Blu operates in India's fragrance and personal care market, where brands compete across mass-market, affordable premium and luxury segments. The company's positioning aims to serve consumers seeking alternatives to lower-priced mass-market products and higher-priced international brands.
The increase in its annualised revenue run rate from Rs 100 crore to Rs 250 crore over six months provides an indication of the pace at which the company has expanded its business. The figure represents an annualised estimate based on its current revenue performance rather than revenue earned over a completed financial year. The company's next phase of growth will depend on its ability to sustain sales momentum, expand distribution and maintain operating efficiency as it reaches more consumers.
Bla Bli Blu's latest milestone places profitability alongside revenue growth as a key development in its business. Its use of e-commerce, quick commerce and marketing partnerships forms part of its strategy to build a larger presence in India's competitive fragrance market.
Udaan, the business-to-business (B2B) e-commerce platform, is targeting an initial public offering (IPO) by late 2027 or early 2028 as it works towards profitability and strengthens its financial performance. The company expects revenue to grow by 10 to 12 percent in FY26, while losses are projected to decline by around 20 percent.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Vaibhav Gupta expects the company to achieve full profitability by the end of 2027. The proposed public listing would mark a significant step for the B2B e-commerce company, which has spent the past three years restructuring its operations and shifting its focus from expansion to sustainable growth.
Udaan has significantly reduced its operating footprint as part of its business restructuring. Previously serving retailers across approximately 80 Indian cities, the company has consolidated its operations into around 16 clusters, with a sharper focus on groceries and essential goods.
The strategy prioritises improving order economics, increasing purchase frequency and generating more revenue from existing retail customers rather than expanding aggressively into new markets. Between the fourth quarter of calendar year 2023 and the first quarter of calendar year 2026, Udaan's revenue grew at a compound annual growth rate of approximately 25 percent. Its contribution margin improved by nearly 500 basis points, while its EBITDA burn declined by around 70 percent.
“We moved beyond scale to focus on market economics and revenue quality: wallet share, purchase frequency and contribution per order,” Gupta said.
The company has also reported progress in improving profitability at the city level, with Bengaluru and several other major operating clusters already generating positive EBITDA.
Udaan's financial performance in FY25 reflected the impact of its restructuring. Revenue declined by 20 percent to Rs 4,561 crore as the company exited selected non-core categories. However, its net loss narrowed by 37 percent to Rs 1,055 crore.
The company has reduced its net losses for three consecutive financial years. Its losses stood at Rs 2,075 crore in FY23 and Rs 1,674.1 crore in FY24 before declining further in FY25. In July 2026, Udaan announced a $160 million recapitalisation involving fresh equity, additional debt and the conversion of debt into equity. The transaction was intended to strengthen its balance sheet and simplify its capital structure. It followed a $114 million Series G financing round in 2025.
Gupta said, “I think the first two or three years we also started doubting ourselves many times. But what was great was that we stayed focused and continued to build the business,” said Gupta. “We started showing that the model was working, and that helped build confidence among our existing and new investors.”
Udaan is also working to increase revenue from private-label products and institutional procurement services. Private labels account for 15 to 25 percent of staples sales across its operating cities. Its horeca360 business serves hotels, restaurants, caterers, and other institutional buyers. In Bengaluru, private labels and HoReCa together contribute around half of the company's revenue, according to the report.
The company has also expanded its distribution network through the acquisition of LYNK Logistics, previously owned by Swiggy, in an all-share transaction valued at Rs 500 crore. Under the deal, Swiggy received an approximately 2.8 percent stake in Udaan and invested an additional Rs 75 crore. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Udaan's distribution capabilities and retail reach in markets that align with its existing operating clusters.
Udaan's immediate priority is to translate improvements in individual markets into consistent profitability across the business. Its operating model places greater emphasis on contribution margins, customer retention, order frequency, basket sizes, procurement efficiency and fulfilment costs. Rather than relying primarily on new customer acquisition and geographical expansion, the company plans to increase its share of existing retailers' procurement spending by encouraging more frequent orders and broader product purchases.
“The biggest opportunity is to win more of existing retailers’ procurement spend, rather than overinvest in customer acquisition or new markets,” Gupta said.
The company sees further growth potential in its existing markets and believes its current cluster-based approach can support expansion without requiring the same level of investment in infrastructure as entering new cities. Udaan's planned IPO will depend on its ability to sustain revenue growth, reduce losses and achieve its profitability target. If the company meets its stated objectives, a listing by late 2027 or early 2028 could provide a public-market milestone for one of India's major B2B e-commerce platforms.
DeVANS Modern Breweries has appointed Vikas Bhatia as Chief Operating Officer (COO) as the Indian alcoholic beverages company looks to strengthen its commercial operations, expand distribution and identify new growth opportunities. Bhatia brings over 30 years of experience across sales, marketing, commercial leadership and market development.
He has held senior positions at Red Bull, SABMiller, Diageo, Radico Khaitan, and Kraft Heinz, spanning the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and alcoholic beverages sectors. In his new role, Bhatia will focus on strengthening DeVANS' commercial execution, improving operational efficiency, developing markets and expanding its retail and on-premise distribution networks. He will also identify opportunities to grow the company's brewing and distilling businesses.
Founded in 1961, DeVANS Modern Breweries has evolved from a liquor bottling business into a manufacturer of beer and premium spirits. The company has expanded its manufacturing footprint from one unit to four under the leadership of Chairman and Managing Director Prem Dewan. Its portfolio includes Godfather beer, Six Fields craft beer, GianChand Indian single malt whisky and Gingalalahu gin. The company operates across beer and spirits, with a focus on strengthening its market presence and expanding distribution in India.
Prem Dewan, Chairman and Managing Director of DeVANS Modern Breweries Limited said, “DeVANS has a legacy spanning more than six decades, and our ambition is to build on that foundation as we take the company into its next phase of growth. Vikas brings extensive experience across leading beverage and FMCG businesses, along with a strong understanding of commercial development and market expansion. We look forward to working with him to strengthen our capabilities, develop our business and to further strengthen DeVANS into one of the premier beverage companies in India.”
Bhatia said, “I am delighted to join DeVANS at an important stage in its journey. The company’s legacy, evolving portfolio and ambition to build stronger brands present an exciting opportunity. I look forward to working with the team to strengthen commercial execution, explore new market opportunities and create a platform for sustainable, long-term growth.”
The appointment comes as DeVANS works to strengthen its presence in India's beer and premium spirits markets. Its growth strategy combines manufacturing capacity, production partnerships, distribution expansion and the development of its beverage portfolio. With Bhatia taking charge of operations, the company aims to strengthen its commercial capabilities and improve execution as it pursues expansion across domestic markets.
Libas, an Indian ethnic wear brand, plans to open nine exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across five cities during the nine days of Navratri as it expands its offline retail network. The move is aimed at increasing the brand's physical presence and strengthening its omnichannel business ahead of the festive shopping season.
The new stores will be located in Bengaluru, Jaipur, Kanpur, Noida and Jabalpur. The expansion follows a year of increased store additions, with Libas opening 28 outlets in FY26, compared with 10 in the previous fiscal year. The company plans to add more than 50 stores in FY27. Libas crossed an annual revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 1,000 crore in March 2026 and is targeting revenue of Rs 1,000 crore in FY27.
Sidhant Keshwani, Founder and CEO, Libas said, “As Libas enters its next phase of growth, offline retail will be an important lever in expanding our consumer reach and strengthening our presence across markets. Our focus is on building a retail network that allows us to scale efficiently, respond to local demand and deliver a consistent brand experience. The nine store openings during Navratri is part of this larger strategy, as we work towards our FY27 growth ambitions.”
The nine outlets will be spread across key retail locations in the five cities. In Bengaluru, stores will open at Airport Road, Jayanagar, Commercial Street and Mantri Mall. Jaipur will have outlets at Pacific Mall and Vaishali Nagar, while the Kanpur store will be located at Z Square Mall. The remaining outlets will open at H&S in Noida and South Avenue Mall in Jabalpur.
The planned additions build on Libas' recent retail expansion as the company works to increase its presence across India's ethnic wear market. The brand's strategy combines its digital-first business with physical stores to reach more consumers and provide additional shopping channels.
With more than 50 new stores planned for FY27, Libas is continuing to invest in offline retail while pursuing its revenue target for the financial year. The Navratri openings form part of this broader expansion plan, with the company looking to strengthen its presence across established and emerging fashion markets.
McCain Foods has entered into an agreement to acquire the frozen potato processing business of Falcon Agrifriz Foods in Gujarat, expanding its manufacturing capacity in India. The transaction will complement McCain’s existing operations in Mehsana and support its plans to meet growing demand for frozen potato products in domestic and international markets. The acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions. Once completed, the deal will add Falcon Agrifriz’s processing facility to McCain’s manufacturing network in India, providing additional capacity and greater operational flexibility.
Falcon Agrifriz operates a purpose-built potato processing facility in Gujarat that manufactures frozen potato products for domestic consumption and export markets. The acquisition is expected to strengthen McCain’s existing production base in Mehsana and support its ability to serve customers across India and key international markets.
Pierre Danet, Regional President, Asia Pacific and South Africa at McCain said, “India continues to be a priority growth market for McCain Foods. This acquisition reflects our confidence in the Indian market and builds on nearly three decades of continued investment in our people, local operations and agricultural partnerships. By strengthening our manufacturing network, we will be better positioned to grow alongside our customers, growers and communities for the long term.”
McCain began its operations in India in 1998 with a team of three and has since expanded its workforce and manufacturing presence. The company now employs more than 940 people directly and works with over 2,500 farmers across the country. The Falcon Agrifriz facility will add to McCain’s existing manufacturing operations in Mehsana, helping the company manage production requirements and serve customers more efficiently. The acquisition will also bring Falcon Agrifriz’s workforce of more than 450 employees and its relationships with over 1,000 farmers across Gujarat into the business, subject to the transaction’s completion.
Parthajeet Patnaik, Vice Chairman, Falcon Agrifriz said, “We are proud of the modern, fully automated processing facility we have built at Falcon Agrifriz in less than two years, and especially proud of the talented employees and growers who have helped bring it to life.”
Manish Tibrewal, Director and CEO, Falcon Agrifriz said, “McCain shares our values and our confidence in the growth potential of India’s frozen food market, As a global leader in frozen potato products, McCain is the right company to build on the strong foundation we have established at Falcon Agrifriz and take the business forward.”
The transaction follows McCain’s recent investment in its Indian operations, including the completion of a CAD 135 million expansion of its existing facilities in Gujarat. The investment created jobs for 110 full-time employees and 150 contract workers, adding to the company’s manufacturing capacity in the country.
Aditya Krishna, Managing Director, McCain Foods India said, “McCain has been part of India’s food and agriculture sector for nearly thirty years and we remain committed to its continued growth. Our success in India has been built alongside our people, growers, customers and communities. We look forward to welcoming Falcon employees and growers to the McCain network and continuing to create local employment opportunities and support regional industrial development as we enter the next phase of our long-term growth in India.”
Snapdeal's Swagotsav Sale, which began on October 4, has recorded a 59 percent increase in fashion units sold compared with the same sale period last year. The number of buyers purchasing fashion products also grew 63 percent, indicating increased demand for apparel during the festive shopping season.
Gen Z shoppers are contributing to this growth, with demand spanning women's Western wear and traditional ethnic clothing. The sales trends indicate that consumers are shopping for both contemporary everyday styles and outfits suited to festive occasions. Women's Western wear categories, including co-ord sets, T-shirts, jeans, and night suits, saw sales double during the measured period. Women's salwar suits also rose by 100 percent, reflecting demand across both Western and traditional apparel categories.
The growth comes as younger shoppers increasingly explore trend-led clothing at affordable prices. The performance of the Swagotsav Sale also points to the role of accessible pricing in attracting consumers looking for fashion options during the festive season. Demand has extended beyond major metropolitan markets. Around 82 percent of orders during the sale came from outside metro cities, highlighting the contribution of shoppers in smaller cities and towns to online fashion sales. The trend also reflects the reach of e-commerce platforms among consumers seeking affordable apparel and a wider selection of products.
Snapdeal has also reported an increase in seller participation during the sale. The number of active transacting sellers in the fashion category rose 94 percent compared with the corresponding period last year. New seller participation recorded triple-digit growth in smaller cities, including Bhilwara, Meerut, Hosur, Kota, Amroha, Alwar and Solapur. The increase in seller activity indicates growing participation from businesses across different parts of India in online fashion retail. For smaller sellers, e-commerce marketplaces provide an additional channel to reach customers beyond their local markets.
Prepaid orders doubled during the sale period, adding to the growth recorded in fashion sales, customer numbers and seller participation.
Ahead of the festive season, Snapdeal has been working with sellers through Project Gati, a 45-day acceleration programme aimed at helping first-time sellers prepare for higher seasonal demand. The initiative includes seller training, AI upgradation, free advertising credits, analytics sharing to support assortment planning and shorter working capital cycles.
Achint Setia, CEO of Snapdeal said, “Gen Z is increasingly buying looks, rather than simply buying clothes for their functional value. From Western wear to ethnicwear and accessories, shoppers are exploring styles that reflect their personality and the occasion. We have organised Swagotsav around this shift, bringing together affordable, trend-led choices that help consumers create their festive looks without stretching their budgets.”
RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group has appointed Harshad Jain as the chief executive officer of its fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) business, effective Monday, according to a company circular.
Jain brings over 35 years of leadership experience spanning aviation, media and entertainment, consumer businesses and telecommunications. He holds a postgraduate diploma in sales and marketing and has worked across multiple industries during his career.
Most recently, Jain served in advisory roles to the boards of several companies, supporting their strategic growth, business transformation and expansion efforts.
Prior to his advisory assignments, Jain was CEO of the non-aeronautical business at Adani Airport Holdings Limited. His previous roles include stints at HT Media Ltd, Bharti Airtel Ltd, World Space India and PepsiCo India, where he gained experience across media, telecommunications, aviation and consumer goods.
As part of his new role, Jain will be based at RPSG House and report to Shashwat Goenka, Vice Chairman of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, according to the company circular.
The appointment brings an experienced business leader to the group's FMCG operations, with a background spanning consumer-facing businesses and corporate leadership.
COCO LENI, the craft-led eyewear brand headquartered in Pilerne, Goa, has opened its first gallery space in Ahmedabad, marking another step in its retail expansion across India.
The Ahmedabad launch reflects the brand’s focus on markets that combine entrepreneurial ambition with a strong appreciation for architecture, textiles and the arts. According to Arjun Sagar, Founder and Creative Director of COCO LENI, the city’s emphasis on growth and innovation makes it a natural fit for the brand.
“While our eyewear is collected by connoisseurs from all over the world, I am particularly inspired by the entrepreneurial energy in Ahmedabad and the city's pride in architecture, textiles and the arts. This spirit of looking forward is what defines COCO LENI, and we are excited to dress Ahmedabad in COCO LENI frames,” said Sagar.
COCO LENI’s collection spans acetate, titanium and handcrafted horn eyewear. Its acetate frames use Mazzucchelli acetate, while its titanium designs draw inspiration from Eastern philosophies of calm and composure. The brand also offers handcrafted horn frames, emphasising durability and craftsmanship.
A key differentiator is the brand’s focus on fit for Indian facial features. While much of the global eyewear market caters to other face shapes, COCO LENI has developed three frame sizes designed to accommodate Indian noses and provide a more suitable fit for Indian customers.
Every COCO LENI frame is designed and manufactured at the brand’s facility in Pilerne, Goa, and undergoes more than 40 production steps before reaching customers.
Sagar brings over two decades of experience gained in the United States and Germany, where he developed his understanding of traditional eyewear craftsmanship. He returned to India to build a brand that combines these principles with contemporary design and a global outlook.
The brand’s customer base comprises individuals who value craftsmanship, detail and understated confidence. Its focus on product quality and design has helped it build a loyal following, including customers who own multiple pieces from its collections.
“Our customers define our products as much as our products define them,” Sagar said.
With the Ahmedabad opening, COCO LENI continues to strengthen its presence in India. The brand currently operates more than 10 stores across Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Goa and Hyderabad, with a Bengaluru store expected to open in November.
Beyond its domestic retail network, COCO LENI has customers in more than 22 countries. The brand is also planning to open its first international flagship store next year to cater to existing overseas demand.
The expansion signals COCO LENI’s focus on building a wider retail presence while retaining its emphasis on Indian craftsmanship, material quality and eyewear designed for Indian consumers.
Nat Habit, an Indian beauty and personal care brand, has raised Rs 142 crore in a Series C funding round led by Trident Growth Partners, with participation from existing investors Bertelsmann India Investments, Mirabilis Investment Trust and Sharrp Ventures. The all-primary funding round also saw investments from new investors Physis Capital and Hero Family Office.
The funding comes as the brand's annualized gross revenue reaches Rs 330 crore. Founded in 2019 by Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal, Nat Habit offers hair care, skin care, body care and baby care products based on its Fresh Ayurveda proposition, combining traditional Ayurvedic principles with modern science. The company said it has served more than 60 lakh households across India.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its product portfolio, strengthen its presence across quick commerce and offline retail channels, and increase its digital reach in Tier II and Tier III markets.
Nat Habit also plans to strengthen its in-house research and development, formulation and manufacturing capabilities to support its product development and Fresh Ayurveda positioning.
Atul Gupta, Managing Partner at Trident Growth Partners, said the firm sees significant growth potential in India's personal care market as consumers increasingly seek natural products for the entire family. He added that Nat Habit had built a differentiated business through its in-house research, formulation and manufacturing capabilities, with the brand reaching a stage where it can scale across online and offline channels.
Swagatika Das, Co-founder of Nat Habit, said the investment would help the company make its products accessible to more households across India.
"Our ambition now is to make our products accessible to many more households across India. This investment marks an important step in that direction, enabling us to expand our product portfolio, strengthen our presence across quick commerce and offline retail, and reach deeper into emerging markets," Das said.
Ajay’s Cafe has launched Barbeque Fries at Rs 70 across all its outlets, expanding its menu with a new flavor featuring smoky, tangy and mildly spicy notes. The launch adds a new variant to the quick-service restaurant (QSR) chain’s fries offering, with the brand focusing on flavor innovation at an accessible price point.
The Barbeque Fries combine a crispy texture with barbeque seasoning, offering customers an alternative to regular fries. The new product is available across the brand’s outlet network.
“Fries are a much-loved part of the quick-service food experience, but customers are increasingly looking for new flavors. With Barbeque Fries, we have launched a flavor that is bold, smoky, tangy and easy to enjoy. We have kept the offering simple and accessible at Rs 70, while ensuring the taste and consistency that our customers have come to expect from Ajay’s Cafe,” said Ajay Solanki, Founder Director, Ajay’s Cafe.
Founded in Navsari, Gujarat, in 2014, Ajay’s Cafe has grown to more than 286 outlets across 67 cities in Gujarat and Rajasthan. Gujarat remains its largest market, while the company is expanding into new geographies.
The brand recently entered Maharashtra with two outlets in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and plans to expand to 30 outlets in the state over the next year.
Ajay’s Cafe operates on a model centered on affordable pricing, a strong supply chain, standardized processes and consistent product quality. Since its inception, the brand has served more than 4.44 crore burgers and 3.07 crore cold coffees, according to the company.
The Barbeque Fries launch adds to the brand’s menu as it continues to grow its store network and expand its reach in the Indian QSR market.
Flipkart recorded 6.3 million concurrent users during the opening hour of its 13th Big Billion Days (TBBD) sale, as the e-commerce platform reported strong demand across smartphones, electronics, appliances, beauty and lifestyle categories. The platform saw over six times more shoppers in the first hour than during a regular hour, while new customer additions grew 34%.
Early Access began at midnight on October 8 for Flipkart Plus and Black members and eligible co-branded credit card customers. The opening phase generated more than 287 million sessions, with shoppers across metro and non-metro markets participating in the festive sale.
Customers from Tier 3 towns and beyond accounted for nearly half of the visits during the first hour, while non-metro markets contributed approximately 60% of demand. Sardulgarh, Panskura, Sheikhpura and Kishanganj emerged as some of the fastest-growing markets during the opening phase.
Product affordability remained a key factor in purchase decisions, particularly in smartphones. One in four customers opted for product exchange, while one in three chose No Cost EMI. Entry-level 5G smartphones priced at last year's levels also attracted buyers.
Large appliances recorded 30% year-on-year growth in the first hour, led by air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines. Tablet sales grew 73%, indicating demand for personal technology upgrades.
Beauty sales increased 42% year-on-year during the opening hour, driven by men's grooming and self-care products. At peak, the platform sold more than 1,600 men's perfume units per minute.
Quick-commerce service Flipkart Minutes recorded a 3.5x increase in order volumes compared with regular days during the opening hour, while new customers grew 11x. Demand extended beyond daily essentials to premium electronics, grooming products and wearables, with Tier 2-plus cities emerging as fast-growing markets.
During Early Access, an iPhone 17 was delivered to a customer in New Delhi in 3.4 minutes through Flipkart Minutes. Other popular purchases included air fryers, laptops and external hard drives.
Content-led shopping also contributed to engagement during Early Access. Flipkart offered more than 1,000 hours of live commerce content and over 500,000 short-format videos, attracting 12.7 million users to its video and live shopping experiences.
Voice Search adoption was particularly strong in Tier 2-plus markets, which accounted for approximately 64% of users of the feature. Lifestyle and makeup products were among the most-searched categories.
Gen Z shoppers showed increased interest in beauty and personal style, with beauty purchases growing 48% and watches increasing 42% among younger consumers. Sneakers, perfumes, skincare, creatine and jeans were among the most-searched products across fashion and personal care.
The festive sale also generated business for sellers across the platform. On the Early Access day, 51% of transacting sellers recorded twice their regular-day business. Sellers in Tier 2-plus markets, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), recorded 2.9x growth.
Bhiwandi, Panipat, Tirupur and Hisar were among the locations driving the increase in seller activity. The opening performance highlights the growing contribution of non-metro markets, affordability-led purchases, quick commerce and digital discovery to India's festive e-commerce demand.
Consumer electronics brand Portronics has launched the Zeno L Mini, a cordless air compression leg massager featuring six customizable massage modes, two pressure levels and a rechargeable battery. Priced at Rs 2,849, the device is designed for home use, relaxation and post-workout recovery.
The Zeno L Mini features a compact wraparound design in a black finish, with Velcro fastening for an adjustable fit. Its portable design allows users to store and carry the device conveniently, while its cordless operation enables use without a continuous power connection.
The massager offers six modes: Calf, Thigh, Upper Arm, Forearm, Recovery and Targeted. Users can choose between low and high pressure settings and select 10-minute or 20-minute massage sessions. Its air compression system operates through an inflate, compress and release cycle.
The device comes with a detachable control unit featuring dedicated buttons for power, massage mode, pressure and timer settings. It is powered by a 2,000mAh rechargeable battery, offering up to 75 minutes of runtime on a single charge. Type-C charging supports recharging, while the cordless format is intended to provide greater flexibility during use.
The Portronics Zeno L Mini has a maximum retail price (MRP) of Rs 5,999 and is listed at Rs 2,849 on the brand’s official website. It comes with a 12-month warranty and is available through Portronics.com, Amazon.in, Flipkart.com and other online and offline retail stores across India.
Vinod Intelligent Cookware, a cookware brand established in 1962, organised a creator-led brand activation in Hyderabad on October 8 in association with Agromech Industries, its retail and modern trade partner in the city. The event brought together more than 50 creators from the food, lifestyle and home categories, with the objective of strengthening brand visibility, increasing consumer engagement and supporting sales growth in the market.
Hosted at Agromech Industries, the activation featured interactive games, quizzes, a live cook-off and hands-on product demonstrations. The initiative provided creators with an opportunity to explore the brand's cookware range and develop content around its products.
The event showcased Vinod Intelligent Cookware's Stainless Steel, Platinum Triply SAS Pro and Freya collections. As part of the live cook-off, 16 shortlisted participants competed in an on-the-spot cooking challenge using the brand's cookware, while other attendees explored the product experience zone. The demonstrations highlighted features such as Freya's titanium-enamel cast iron construction and anti-rust coating, along with the triply-constructed SAS Pro.
The activation forms part of Vinod's efforts to expand its presence in Hyderabad, which the company considers a key growth market. The brand operates through a distributor network, retail and modern trade partners, a dedicated sales team, and an established consumer base in the city. It aims to become the leading cookware brand in Hyderabad and capture a significant share of the local market.
Arjun Agarwal, Director- Business Development, Vinod Cookware India Pvt. Ltd. said, “Hyderabad is an important growth market for us, and we see a strong opportunity to build on the trust we have established with consumers and our retail partners here. This activation allowed us to bring the brand closer to consumers through an experience that was interactive, hands-on and relevant to the way people discover products today. Our association with Agromech gives us a strong local retail foundation, while the creator community helps us extend the product experience into real kitchens and consumer conversations. This is an important step in our journey towards building a leading cookware brand in Hyderabad.”
Aashi Jain, Director- Marketing & E-commerce, Agromech Industries shared, “At Agromech, we aim to bring our customers greater choice and innovations that add value to everyday life. Our association with Vinod Cookware reflects this through its wide cookware range and new technologies designed to make cooking more convenient and efficient. This activation allows participants to experience these benefits firsthand through live demonstrations and hands-on activities. Such interactions encourage questions, deepen product understanding, and help us build a stronger connection with our customers.”
The event also focused on extending consumer engagement through social media. Participating creators, primarily based in Hyderabad, were expected to publish a reel and a story each, while on-camera testimonials were recorded during the activation to support further digital engagement.
The initiative follows Vinod Intelligent Cookware's earlier experiential campaigns, including “Cook with SAS Pro” in Mumbai and “Hue Are You In The Kitchen” in Pune with Chef Nehal Karkera. While those initiatives centred on chef-led product experiences, the Hyderabad event adopted a creator-led approach combining product demonstrations, interactive activities, and social media content.
SABAQI, a Made-in-India premium furniture startup, has formally entered India's premium furniture market following its launch at Dialogue Udaipur, held from October 1 to 4. Founded by three industry veterans, the company is targeting approximately Rs 80-100 crore in project closures over the coming year as it expands its presence across India.
Founded by Hitesh Sakariya, Nakul Kanchhal and Dheeraj Gehani, SABAQI brings together experience in furniture, manufacturing, luxury retail and business expansion. The founders have more than two decades of industry experience and have previously built or led businesses, including Kuche7 and Hästens.
The company is developing a business model that combines collection-based furniture with customisation. Instead of producing entirely bespoke pieces for every client, SABAQI offers furniture based on a defined design language, with flexibility to modify materials, finishes, proportions and other specifications to suit individual spaces. This approach is intended to give architects, interior designers and customers greater scope to customise furniture without relying entirely on one-off production.
Manufacturing is central to SABAQI's operating model. Its setup integrates design, engineering and production, with in-house capabilities across metalwork, carpentry, upholstery, painting and stonework. Quality checks at different stages of production are intended to maintain consistency in materials, finishes, detailing and execution. The company also draws on more than 10 years of manufacturing experience within its leadership team's operations.
Nakul Kanchhal, Co-Founder of SABAQI, said the company was established to address the gap between highly customised furniture and standardised collections that offer limited flexibility. “For years, we have seen architects and clients looking for furniture that is distinctive in design, precise in detailing and genuinely suited to the space they are creating. Yet when they wanted something beyond the familiar, they often had to look outside India. The choice was frequently between highly bespoke furniture, which can be difficult to execute consistently, and collection-led products that leave little room for adaptation. SABAQI was born from that gap. We are building a system where design, engineering, manufacturing and craftsmanship work together from the beginning. Our in-house capabilities across metal, carpentry, upholstery, paint and stone, combined with quality checks at every stage, allow us to bring greater consistency and control to the process.”
Kanchhal said the company's approach also focuses on product durability, functionality and timely project execution. “Having spent years in this industry, we know that beautiful furniture alone is not enough. It has to work, last, arrive when promised and feel like it belongs to the person and the space it was made for. For us, Made in India is not simply about where the furniture is manufactured; it is about building the capability to design, make and solve problems better from within India. Our ambition is therefore much larger than building another successful Indian furniture company. We want SABAQI to become an Indian design and manufacturing brand that can stand confidently alongside the best in the world; not by imitating what already exists, but by developing our own language, our own standards and, ultimately, a legacy of our own.”
SABAQI currently has the capacity to manage an average of 20-25 projects simultaneously. Individual projects start at approximately Rs 50 lakh, depending on their scope and client requirements. The company is also developing approximately 150-200 stock-keeping units (SKUs) during 2026-27. Alongside its planned collections, it will continue to work with architects and designers on customised furniture requirements.
The manufacturing-led model is intended to address challenges in the premium furniture segment, including variations in materials, finishes, detailing and ergonomics, as well as extended project timelines. SABAQI aims to support architects and end customers through coordinated design and production processes.
As part of its retail expansion strategy, SABAQI plans to establish five stores by 2026-27 while continuing to execute projects across India. The company is also open to franchise partnerships as it develops its distribution network and physical retail presence. Its launch at Dialogue Udaipur marked its formal introduction to India's architecture and design community. The private event, held from October 1 to 4, brought together approximately 45-50 architects from across the country, providing a platform for the company to present its furniture collections and manufacturing capabilities to a design-focused, high-net-worth audience.
With its project pipeline, planned product range and store expansion strategy, SABAQI aims to build an Indian premium furniture business around design, manufacturing and customisation. The company is looking to strengthen domestic capabilities while developing products that can compete in international markets.
British-heritage men's footwear brand Thomas Crick, manufactured and marketed in India by Mirza International Limited, recorded sales of Rs 11.18 crore in FY26, marking continued growth since entering the Indian market in October 2023. The brand is targeting sales of more than Rs 20 crore in FY27 as it expands its presence across e-commerce platforms and organised retail.
Thomas Crick reported revenue of Rs 28.10 lakh during its initial six-month operating period in FY24, which increased to Rs 5.70 crore in FY25. Sales more than doubled in FY26, taking the brand's revenue to Rs 11.18 crore. This represents nearly 36-fold growth since its entry into India.
Initially operating through a digital-first model, Thomas Crick established its presence on e-commerce platforms, including Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra. The brand has now expanded into offline retail through Reliance Trends, marking a step towards building an omnichannel business in India.
The move is expected to increase the brand's accessibility and enable it to reach consumers who prefer shopping at physical stores. The expansion also provides an opportunity to strengthen its visibility beyond its existing online customer base as it works towards its FY27 sales target.
Thomas Crick's India business combines British-inspired footwear designs with domestic manufacturing capabilities. Mirza International, an established Indian leather and footwear manufacturer, manufactures and markets the brand in the country, supporting its positioning in the accessible-premium segment.
Its product portfolio includes Chelsea boots, formal lace-up shoes, loafers and casual leather footwear. The collection focuses on heritage-inspired designs suited to contemporary consumer preferences, with pricing positioned below the luxury footwear segment.
The brand's expansion into organised retail comes as it looks to build on its online business and increase its reach in India's branded footwear market. Its performance across e-commerce and physical retail channels will be important to achieving its projected sales growth.
With its entry into Reliance Trends, Thomas Crick is looking to strengthen its distribution network while broadening its consumer base. The company expects to cross Rs 20 crore in sales in FY27, with growth dependent on the performance of its existing digital channels and its expanding offline presence.
The brand's progression from Rs 28.10 lakh in its first six months of operations to Rs 11.18 crore in FY26 reflects its growth since entering India and its transition towards a wider omnichannel retail strategy.
Avenue Supermarts, the company that owns and operates D-Mart, reported an 18.4 percent year-on-year increase in standalone revenue from operations to Rs 19,206.18 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. The retailer had recorded revenue from operations of Rs 16,218.79 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year, according to a regulatory filing released.
“Standalone Revenue from operations for the quarter ended (QE) September 30, 2026, stood at Rs 19,206.18 crore,” the company said in its quarterly update.
D-Mart's standalone revenue also increased 4.7 percent compared with the preceding quarter. Avenue Supermarts reported revenue of Rs 18,343.49 crore for the April-June quarter of FY27. The latest figures indicate continued growth in the retailer's revenue as it operates across multiple markets in India's organised retail sector.
As of September 30, 2026, D-Mart had a total of 518 stores across its network. The count includes its outlet in Sanpada, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, which is currently closed to customers for reconstruction. Promoted by Radhakishan Damani and his family, D-Mart sells everyday household essentials and personal care products through its retail stores.
The retailer has a presence across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, the National Capital Region, Tamil Nadu, Punjab and Rajasthan. Avenue Supermarts' latest revenue update provides an indication of the company's performance in the September quarter, ahead of its detailed financial results.
Amazon India’s Great Indian Festival 2026 recorded a 100 percent year-on-year increase in the number of products ordered during its opening 12 hours, with customers from every Indian pin code placing orders across categories, including smartphones, consumer electronics, fashion, beauty and home appliances, according to the company.
The early performance highlights demand during India's festive shopping season, with premium products recording higher sales across several categories. Amazon said the event also saw increased customer participation across metropolitan areas and smaller towns.
Smartphones and consumer electronics contributed to the increase in shopping volumes, while large home appliances also recorded higher demand. Sales of large appliances reached 50 times their regular daily levels during the opening period. Premium front-load washing machines with capacities of 9 kg and above sold at 80 times their usual daily volume. Refrigerators and dryers recorded sales at 60 times their regular levels, indicating demand for higher-capacity appliances during the festive sale.
Fashion sales during the opening period reached seven times the level of a regular day, with seven pairs of shoes sold every second. Beauty products also recorded significant demand, accounting for one in every four products purchased during the first 12 hours of the sale. The performance across these categories reflects the breadth of demand during Amazon's annual festive sale, which covers products ranging from everyday essentials to premium electronics and lifestyle goods.
Amazon reported receiving orders from every pin code in India during the opening 12 hours of the Great Indian Festival 2026. The company also highlighted faster deliveries, with millions of orders reaching customers within hours. In more than 120 cities served by Amazon Now, one in every two products was delivered within minutes.
The platform also reported greater use of payment offers and affordability options during the opening period. One in every two customers used equated monthly instalments (EMIs), while one in every three units purchased received cashback benefits. Prime members recorded savings of more than 100 percent compared with the corresponding period last year, supported by member-exclusive offers.
The opening performance places Amazon's Great Indian Festival among the key events in India's e-commerce festive sales calendar. The coming weeks will provide a clearer picture of whether the early increase in order volumes translates into sustained demand across product categories and seller segments.
P N Gadgil Jewellers reported a 22.4 percent year-on-year revenue increase in the second quarter of FY27, supported by growth in its retail and franchise businesses. The jewellery retailer plans to open around 23 additional stores during the financial year, taking its total network to approximately 103 outlets by the end of FY27.
Retail revenue increased 31.1 percent during the quarter, while same-store sales growth stood at 25.5 percent. The franchise business also recorded growth of 34.7 percent, reflecting higher revenue from the company's retail network.
However, e-commerce revenue declined 83.6 percent year-on-year. The company attributed the decline to a strategic shift away from lower-margin gold coin sales towards higher-margin jewellery products. Gold coin and bar sales accounted for 15.8 percent of retail revenue during Q2FY27, compared with 23.3 percent in the corresponding quarter last year. PNG Jewellers recorded growth across its key jewellery categories during the quarter. Gold revenue increased 23.5 percent year-on-year, while diamond revenue grew 21 percent and silver revenue rose 12 percent.
The share of studded jewellery in retail sales increased to 11.8 percent, compared with 9 percent in the year-ago quarter. In northern India, the studded jewellery ratio stood at 17.4 percent. Meanwhile, old gold exchange accounted for 38 percent of sales, up from 29 percent in Q2FY26.
The company opened two stores during Q2FY27, including a Legacy-format outlet in Gurugram and a YOOU store at Amanora Mall in Pune. As of September 30, 2026, PNG Jewellers operated 80 stores, comprising 79 outlets in India and one in the United States. PNG Jewellers aims to expand its network to about 103 stores by the end of FY27, driven primarily by franchise-led growth across its Legacy and YOOU formats.
The company has secured commitments for 10 additional stores, including six Legacy outlets and four YOOU stores. It is also evaluating further opportunities, particularly across northern and central India. The Ayodhya store is expected to open by mid-October, followed by the Prayagraj outlet in early November. The retailer has also transitioned its LiteStyle brand to YOOU as part of its focus on contemporary, lightweight jewellery. The company stated that its Q2FY27 revenue figures are subject to a limited review by statutory auditors, with a detailed update to follow after board approval.
V-Mart Retail plans to increase apparel prices by 3 percent to 5 percent in the October-December quarter of FY27 (Q3FY27) to manage rising raw material costs, according to Anand Agarwal, Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer of the value-fashion retailer. The company had kept prices unchanged during the July-September quarter (Q2FY27), despite several other retailers raising apparel prices by 10 percent to 15 percent. The decision was aimed at retaining its value-conscious customer base amid increasing input costs.
During the quarter, V-Mart Retail reported 18 percent growth in total revenue and a 3 percent increase in same-store sales. Agarwal said the planned single-digit price adjustment would help the company manage cost pressures. He added that further price increases could be necessary from the fourth quarter onward if input costs, particularly those influenced by oil prices, remain elevated.
On the demand front, V-Mart Retail reported strong early-quarter footfall, supported by the beginning of Durga Puja festivities in eastern India. The shift in the festive season from Q2 to Q3 had a slight impact on the previous quarter's performance and could also put pressure on margins. Despite these factors, the retailer expects its overall performance to remain stable and broadly in line with the previous year. V-Mart Retail is scheduled to announce its full profitability results in early November.
The planned price revision comes as apparel retailers navigate higher raw material costs while balancing pricing decisions with demand from price-sensitive consumers. For V-Mart Retail, the proposed increase reflects an effort to manage cost inflation while maintaining its positioning in India's value-fashion retail market.
PC Jeweller Ltd has reported a 28 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue for the quarter ended September 2026, supported by healthy consumer demand in the jewellery sector. According to a regulatory filing, the jewellery retailer and manufacturer delivered strong growth during the July-September quarter of FY27 while also achieving a major financial milestone by becoming debt-free.
The company had previously announced that it had cleared outstanding dues to all 14 consortium banks, eliminating debt of approximately Rs 3,000 crore. In September 2024, PC Jeweller had opted for a one-time settlement (OTS) arrangement to resolve its outstanding bank liabilities. During the quarter, the company also received remittances of Rs 142 crore from outstanding export debtors, further supporting its financial position and liquidity.
The company said, “During the September quarter, the company achieved debt-free status after successful repayment of outstanding debt of all the banks, with all repayments completed ahead of the scheduled due dates. With no bank debts outstanding, the company will be saving on the interest cost in the future, which will positively impact its bottomline and strengthen its balance sheet.”
The debt repayment is expected to reduce future interest expenses and improve profitability, while strengthening the company's overall financial health. PC Jeweller operates nearly 50 retail jewellery stores across major cities in India and continues to serve consumers across gold jewellery, diamond jewellery, wedding jewellery, and other precious jewellery categories.
The latest business update reflects improving operational performance for the company, supported by strong jewellery demand and a significantly strengthened balance sheet following the completion of its debt repayment programme.
Jubilant FoodWorks Ltd, the operator of Domino’s Pizza in India and several international markets, reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 26,087 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, registering an 11.9 percent year-on-year increase. According to the company’s provisional business update filed with the BSE and NSE, standalone revenue from operations grew 11.6 percent year-on-year to Rs 18,858 million during the second quarter of FY27.
The company reported varied performance across its operating markets during the quarter. Domino’s India recorded like-for-like (LFL) sales growth of 4.1 percent, reflecting growth from existing stores. Meanwhile, Domino’s Eurasia reported a like-for-like sales decline of 2.1 percent after accounting for Ind AS 29 adjustments. Jubilant FoodWorks continued to expand its store network during the quarter, adding a net 108 stores across its businesses. The total network reached 3,820 stores as of September 30, 2026.
Domino’s Pizza India contributed the majority of the expansion, with 88 new stores added during the quarter. The brand’s network increased to 2,601 outlets nationwide. Domino’s Eurasia added three stores, taking its total store count to 798 outlets.
The group’s retail footprint includes both company-owned and franchise-operated stores across four brands and six international markets. The company also stated that the Dunkin’ business has been classified as discontinued operations in both the current and previous reporting periods.
Jubilant FoodWorks noted that the figures remain provisional and are subject to a limited review by the company’s statutory auditors. The latest update reflects continued growth in the company’s foodservice business, supported by revenue expansion and an ongoing focus on store additions across key markets.
Amazon has announced a fresh round of job cuts, primarily affecting its Stores division, which oversees the company's core e-commerce and retail operations. The latest workforce reduction impacts employees across the United States, India, and the United Kingdom as the e-commerce giant continues efforts to realign its business structure with current priorities.
According to reports, fewer than 1,000 white-collar employees have been affected by the latest layoffs. The move comes during Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days shopping event, one of the company's major annual sales campaigns. The latest cuts are part of a broader restructuring exercise that follows a larger workforce reduction programme launched last year, which resulted in approximately 30,000 job cuts across various business units.
An Amazon spokesperson said, "We've adjusted parts of our Stores business because we believe this structure will better enable us to deliver on our priorities."
Reports indicate that teams within customer service, selling partner services, and other retail-related functions may have been impacted as part of the restructuring. Employees in India were among those affected by the latest round of layoffs.
Amazon founder and Executive Chairman Jeff Bezos said the ongoing reductions were linked to aggressive hiring during the pandemic period, when online shopping demand surged significantly. Referring to the previous round of layoffs, Bezos noted, "People were staying home and they were ordering, and it was an incredible, stressful period for us, by the way. The whole team worked extremely hard and did so much, but we really grew our head count."
The development highlights the continued focus among global technology and e-commerce companies on optimizing costs, improving operational efficiency, and restructuring teams amid changing market conditions and growing investments in areas such as artificial intelligence and automation.
Jewellery retailer Senco Gold and Diamonds reported a strong business performance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, with total revenue rising 31 percent year-on-year, supported by festive demand, growth in lightweight jewellery sales, and continued momentum across its retail and digital channels. The positive update also lifted the company's shares, which gained up to 6 percent during trading on Thursday.
The company said consumer demand remained resilient during the second quarter despite elevated gold prices. At the retail level, revenue grew 29 percent year-on-year, while same-store sales growth stood at 19 percent, reflecting strong demand from existing customers.
For the first half of FY27, Senco Gold reported total revenue growth of 48 percent, while retail revenue increased 40 percent. The company also crossed Rs 5,000 crore in revenue during H1FY27 and achieved trailing twelve-month sales of over Rs 10,000 crore. The jewellery brand recorded a 31 percent increase in diamond jewellery revenue during the quarter. Its stud ratio improved to 12.2 percent from 11.6 percent in the first half, indicating growing consumer interest in studded jewellery categories.
Senco Gold expanded its retail network by opening six new showrooms during the quarter, including three company-owned stores and three franchise outlets. This took its total showroom count to 215 stores across India. The company plans to add another 10 to 12 stores in the second half of FY27 as part of its retail expansion strategy.
Digital commerce continued to be a key growth driver, with e-commerce and digital channel sales rising 53 percent year-on-year. The company attributed growth to festive occasions including Rakhi, Janmashtami, Onam, Ganesh Chaturthi, Independence Day, and Ratha Yatra, which supported jewellery purchases during the quarter.
Looking ahead, Senco Gold expects demand to remain strong in the second half of FY27, driven by the wedding season and festivals such as Dhanteras, Diwali, Durga Puja, Karwa Chauth, Chhath Puja, and Christmas. The company also expects improving rural sentiment and post-monsoon demand to support jewellery consumption in India. Despite continued volatility in gold prices, Senco Gold said organized jewellery retailers remain well-positioned to benefit from consumer demand through product innovation, lightweight jewellery collections, and an expanding retail footprint.
Sky Gold and Diamonds Ltd, a jewellery manufacturer and exporter, has completed the acquisition of 100 percent equity shares of Purvi Gems and Jewellery (India) Private Limited, strengthening its position in the lightweight, uncut, and studded jewellery segments. The acquisition was completed on October 7, 2026, for a cash consideration of Rs 9 crore.
According to the company, the transaction was valued at 1.5 times Purvi Gems’ book value as of March 31, 2026, and does not involve any related-party interests. Sky Gold stated that neither its promoters nor promoter group entities have any stake in Purvi Gems. Following the acquisition, the existing management team of Purvi Gems will continue to oversee operations, supporting business continuity and integration efforts.
Purvi Gems specializes in lightweight, uncut, and Precia jewellery categories, segments that have witnessed increasing demand in domestic markets, particularly South India, as well as international markets. Through the acquisition, Sky Gold aims to diversify its product portfolio, strengthen its export business, and expand its presence in higher-margin studded jewellery categories.
The company expects the acquisition to provide access to approximately 100 kg of monthly jewellery sales while enhancing opportunities for cross-selling through Sky Gold’s existing customer network. It also sees potential to strengthen exports, particularly in the Middle East, where demand for specialized jewellery products remains strong.
According to the company, the acquisition is expected to support its long-term growth strategy by expanding capabilities in value-added jewellery categories and improving its overall product mix. Sky Gold highlighted that Purvi Gems is expected to contribute to a business capable of generating annual revenue of approximately Rs 1,600 crore to Rs 1,800 crore over the next two to three years, while also adding established customer relationships, manufacturing expertise, and an experienced workforce.
The transaction follows a series of acquisitions completed by Sky Gold in recent years, including Sparkling Chains Pvt Ltd, Starmangalsutra Pvt Ltd, Speed Bangles Pvt Ltd, and Shri Rishabh Gold. The company said these acquisitions have helped expand its manufacturing capabilities, broaden its product portfolio, and strengthen its market position across jewellery categories.
Mangesh Chauhan, Managing Director, Sky Gold and Diamonds Ltd said, "Strategic acquisitions have been an important driver of Sky Gold's growth and value creation journey. Our disciplined approach to identifying and integrating businesses has helped us expand capabilities, diversify our product portfolio, improve operating efficiencies and strengthen profitability. Past acquisitions have contributed meaningfully to our scale and growth while creating long-term value for stakeholders. The acquisition of Purvi Gems is another step in this direction. The business brings complementary capabilities in the lightweight uncut and studded jewellery segments, an established customer base and a skilled team.
