title: Shiprocket IPO: E-commerce Enablement Firm's Public Issue Booked 56% On First Day Of Subscription, Check Details
content:
Summary of this article
- Shiprocket IPO reached 56 percent subscription on day one.
- Retail investors led demand by booking their quota twice.
- Current grey market premium signals a strong listing gain.
The initial public offering (IPO) of Shiprocket opened for subscription on August 12. The company's public issue is slated to close for subscription on August 14. On the first day of subscription, trends in grey market premium (GMP) for the company’s shares remained high. Here are some key details of the public issue which applicants should know before applying for the IPO.
Shiprocket IPO Subscription
The issue has been subscribed 56 per cent so far on the first day of subscription. Applicants across categories placed bids for approximately 52.98 million shares against the net offer of 94.43 million shares set aside for the public.
Employees of the company have a reserved quota of 1,20,481 shares. So far, employees of Shiprocket have applied for 4,05,174 shares, booking their quota 3.36 times.
Retail investors are driving the demand for the company’s shares on the first day of subscription, as they booked their quota 2.11 times. Retail investors applied for 36.54 million shares compared to the 17.33 million shares reserved for the category.
Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed their quota of 61 per cent as they applied for 15.94 million shares compared to 26 million shares reserved for them. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) have 50.09 million shares reserved for them following the anchor investor allocation. So far, QIBs have applied for 82,082 shares of the company.
Shiprocket IPO GMP
Shares of Shiprocket are currently commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 32 above the upper end of the price band. Based on the upper price band of Rs 97 and the current GMP trends, the shares are expected to list at Rs 129 apiece, indicating an estimated listing premium of 32.99 per cent. However, investors must note that GMP is an unofficial market indicator and does not guarantee actual listing performance.
Shiprocket IPO: Anchor Investors
E-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket has raised Rs 727.41 crore from anchor investors. The anchor investment round took place on August 11. Shiprocket has allotted 75 million equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 97 apiece, the upper end of its price band. Some of the key investors who participated in the anchor round included SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Nomura, and Goldman SachsAsset Management.
Shiprocket IPO Offer Size, Listing Date, Price Band
Shiprocket IPO issue size aggregates to Rs 1,617.48 crore and is a combination of a fresh issue of 91.3 million shares aggregating to Rs 885.50 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 75.5 million shares aggregating to Rs 731.98 crore.
The price band has been fixed at Rs 92 to Rs 97 per share. Retail individual investors (RIIs) can apply for the e-commerce company's public issue by placing bids for 154 shares or 1 lot, aggregating to a minimum investment of Rs 14,938 at the upper price band.
Shiprocket will finalise the share allotment status of the public issue on August 17. Successful applicants will receive shares of Shiprocket in their demat accounts on August 18. Refunds will be issued for unsuccessful applicants on August 18 as well. Shares of Shiprocket will tentatively list on the BSE and NSE on August 19.
Shiprocket: Key Financials
Shiprocket’s total income for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, stood at Rs 2,077.42 crore, up by 24 per cent year on year compared to Rs 1,674.82 crore. The company posted a net loss for the same period of Rs 79.25 crore, compared to a net loss of Rs 74.45 crore in the preceding fiscal. The net worth of the company grew by 2.21 per cent to Rs 1,524.29 crore compared to Rs 1,491.23 crore in the preceding fiscal.
Shiprocket IPO: Reservation
A major part of the public issue has been set aside for QIBs. As much as 10 per cent of the net offer size is reserved for the retail category, while 15 per cent has been set aside for NIIs. The remaining 75 per cent is allocated to QIBs.
Shiprocket: Promoters
Shiprocket operates with no identifiable promoters. All pre-issue holdings are distributed among existing shareholders rather than a distinct promoter group.
Shiprocket IPO: Objective
The company plans to use the net proceeds of the public issue to fund investment in the growth of Shiprocket platforms, including marketing initiatives primarily for the emerging business and for the core business. The proceeds will also be used for investment in technology infrastructure, repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings, funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions, and for general corporate purposes.
About Shiprocket
Shiprocket is an Indian e-commerce enablement company which provides technology-led solutions which help micro, small and medium enterprises, direct-to-consumer brands, and large retailers manage. The company initially started as a shipping platform and now provides domestic and international shipping software, fulfilment centres, omnichannel commerce solutions, and marketing tools.

title: Shiprocket IPO: From Issue Details to Financials; Here’s What You Need to Know
content:
Synopsis: Shiprocket Limited's ₹1,617.48 crore IPO opens on August 12, 2026. The company plans to utilize the proceeds for platform expansion, marketing initiatives, technology infrastructure, debt repayment, and future growth, supported by its leading e-commerce enablement platform and expanding merchant ecosystem.
Shiprocket Limited is launching its Initial Public Offering (IPO) to raise funds for expanding shiprocket platforms, repaying borrowings, and reducing interest costs. The size of the IPO totals up to Rs. 1,617.48 crore, which includes the fresh offer of 9.13 crore equity shares for Rs. 885.50 crore and 7.55 crore shares OFS for Rs. 731.98 crore.
The share issue price of Shiprocket Limited ranges between Rs. 92 and 97. The IPO will commence subscription from August 12, 2026, to August 14, 2026. The shares will be listed on the NSE and BSE on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Here's everything you need to know.
GMP of Shiprocket Limited IPO
As of August 12th, 2026, the shares of Shiprocket Limited in the grey market were trading at a 30.93 percent premium. The shares in the Grey Market traded at Rs. 127. This gives it a premium of Rs. 30 per share over the cap price of Rs. 97.
Overview of Shiprocket Limited
Shiprocket Limited was incorporated in 2011 and operates as a technology-driven e-commerce enablement company. The company helps MSMEs, D2C brands, and large retailers manage and grow their online businesses. According to the Redseer Report, Shiprocket was India's largest new-age end-to-end e-commerce enablement platform by revenue in FY25.
The company was initially founded as a firm dealing in shipping solutions and later diversified into other services. Its main platform offers shipping services within the country and the solution includes order tracking, fast pick up, secure delivery, weigh confirmation, and improved cash on delivery transactions.
Over the years, Shiprocket has diversified into cargo and fulfilment services, cross-border shipping, advertising solutions, and merchant-focused products. Through its Emerging Business segment, the company offers tools that help merchants improve customer conversion, increase sales, and scale their operations efficiently.
In addition, Shiprocket also provides international logistics services to all important countries worldwide, such as the USA, UK, Canada, Europe, and Singapore. In FY26, the company catered to customers from 146 countries. Its revenue is generated mostly via usage basis, where payments from merchants are made according to shipments, transactions, and orders processed by the firm.
Promoters of Shiprocket Limited
Shiprocket Limited is a professionally managed company, without any individual or group of individuals who can be considered to be the promoters of the organization. The organization is run by its management team that includes the founders of the organization, viz., Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor, and Vishesh Khurana.
Selling Shareholders of Shiprocket Limited
The Offer for Sale in the Shiprocket Limited IPO comprises shares being sold by existing investor shareholders and founders. LR India Fund, I S.a.r.l. SICAV-RAIF is the largest selling shareholder and will offer equity shares aggregating up to Rs. 271.70 crore. Tribe Capital III, LLC – Series 1 will sell shares aggregating up to Rs. 120 crore, while MCP3 SPV LLC will offer shares worth up to Rs. 55.53 crore.
Other investor selling shareholders include Moore Strategic Ventures, LLC, which will offer shares aggregating up to Rs. 51.35 crore, Agility International Investment L.L.C. with shares worth up to Rs. 21.15 crore, and 500 Startups III, L.P., which will sell shares aggregating up to Rs. 16.29 crore.
Among the individual selling shareholders, Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel will each offer shares aggregating up to Rs. 6.10 crore. Vishesh Khurana will sell shares worth up to Rs. 2 crore through the Offer for Sale.
Lead Managers of Shiprocket Limited IPO
The Book Running Lead Managers to the issue are Axis Capital Limited, BofA Securities India Limited, JM Financial Limited, and Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Limited. These institutions are managing the public issue process and coordinating the IPO. KFin Technologies Limited has been appointed as the registrar to the issue and will handle IPO application processing, share allotment, refunds, and other investor-related services.
Objectives of the IPO Offer
Shiprocket Limited aims to deploy the net proceeds from the fresh issue for several development purposes. Specifically, the firm will use Rs. 365.60 crore for the growth of the platforms by investing in marketing activities related to the firm’s Emerging Business and Core Business segments.
On the other hand, Rs. 205.80 crore will be used for marketing activities in both Emerging Business and Core Business segments, and Rs. 159.80 crore will be spent on strengthening the technological infrastructure of the platforms.
The company will also allocate Rs. 210 crore towards the repayment or prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings, including accrued interest. The remaining proceeds will be utilized for funding inorganic growth through potential acquisitions and for general corporate purposes, supporting the company's long-term expansion strategy.
Financial Analysis of Shiprocket Limited
Coming to financial highlights, Shiprocket Limited reported revenue from operations of Rs. 2,024.14 crore in FY26, compared to Rs. 1,632.01 crore in FY25, representing a growth of 24.03 percent. The company's net loss increased slightly from Rs. 74.45 crore in FY25 to Rs. 79.25 crore in FY26.
In terms of return ratios, the company's RoNW and ROCE stand at -5.20 percent and -2.65 percent, respectively. Shiprocket Limited has an earnings per share (EPS) of Rs. -1.23, and its price-to-book value ratio is 4.05x.
Shiprocket Limited Vs Peers
Shiprocket Limited reported revenue from operations of Rs. 2,024.14 crore. The company reported a basic and diluted EPS of Rs. (1.23) and a Return on Net Worth (RoNW) of (5.20) percent. The company's net asset value (NAV) per share stood at Rs. 23.96.
In comparison, Unicommerce eSolutions Limited reported revenue from operations of Rs. 204.34 crore, with a basic EPS of Rs. 1.79, a diluted EPS of Rs. 1.78, and a RoNW of 10.60 percent. The company reported a net asset value (NAV) per share of Rs. 17.17.
Strengths of Shiprocket Limited
- Technology-driven platform simplifies logistics and commerce operations for merchants.
- Large merchant network provides scale and recurring business opportunities.
- Comprehensive ecosystem covers shipping, fulfillment, payments, and customer engagement.
- Strong brand recognition among India's growing digital commerce businesses.
- Diversified service offerings reduce dependence on a single revenue stream.
Weaknesses of Shiprocket Limited
- Business operates in a highly competitive e-commerce technology market.
- Growth depends significantly on continued expansion of online commerce.
- Technology investments require substantial capital and ongoing expenditure.
- Changes in logistics costs may impact overall operating performance.
- Regulatory changes could affect digital commerce and platform operations.
Conclusion
Shiprocket Limited IPO gives the investor access to the burgeoning market in India for enabling e-commerce. The company has put in place a very robust platform that enables merchants to handle their logistics, fulfillment, payments, and customer engagement via its technology platform. It is well positioned for future growth due to the support of the large merchant network, the technology prowess, and the increasing use of digital commerce. The investor needs to assess its finances, valuation, growth, and risk carefully before investing.

SUMMARY
Shiprocket on Tuesday raised ₹727.41 crore from anchor investors ahead of the public issue. The company allotted 7.5 crore equity shares to anchor investors at ₹97 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band, according to a circular uploaded on the BSE website.
The company allotted 7.5 crore equity shares to anchor investors at ₹97 apiece. Representative image. Source: Unsplash
The three-day initial public offering (IPO) of e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket Ltd is scheduled to open on Wednesday, August 12. The company on Tuesday raised ₹727.41 crore from anchor investors ahead of the public issue.
Among the investors participating in the anchor book were New York State Teachers Retirement System, managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Nomura Funds Ireland Public Ltd Company, Societe Generale, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, Tata AIA Life Insurance Company and Axis Max Life Insurance.
Other investors on the list were SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund and Bandhan Mutual Fund.
It must be noted that Shiprocket has trimmed the size of its IPO from the ₹2,342.3 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus filed in December 2025.
The issue comprises a fresh issuance of equity shares worth up to ₹885.50 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares aggregating up to ₹732 crore.
The lot size is 154 shares. At the upper price band of ₹97 per share, the minimum investment required for retail investors is ₹14,938 per lot.
Existing shareholders, including Lightrock, Tribe Capital, Moore Strategic Ventures, Agility International Investment, Gautam Kapoor, Saahil Goel and Vishesh Khurana, will sell shares through the OFS.
At the upper end of the price band, Shiprocket will command a post-issue market valuation of about ₹7,058 crore, while at the lower end, the valuation has been pegged at ₹6,739 crore.
As much as 75% of the offer has been reserved for Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), 15% for Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) and the remaining 10% for retail investors.
The company had filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI through the confidential pre-filing route in May and subsequently received the regulator's approval in November to launch the public issue.
Axis Capital, BofA Securities, JM Financial and Kotak Mahindra Capital Company are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.
The company's shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE on August 19.
According to news reports, Shiprocket plans to deploy a significant portion of the IPO proceeds towards artificial intelligence (AI), as it looks to transform its Indian e-commerce (e-commerce) enablement platform into a broader operating system for merchants.
The company aims to enable merchants to manage their businesses through conversational commands instead of using multiple software tabs, while also deploying AI internally to reduce the time spent on data collection and manual tasks.
Goel said that, after debt repayment, most of the IPO proceeds will be directed towards the company’s faster-growing emerging business, including technology and sales and marketing.
The emerging business generated revenue of ₹538.7 crore in financial year 2025-26 (FY26), compared with around ₹1,485.4 crore from the core business during the same period. According to Goel, the emerging business is growing at around 65%.
Backed by marquee investors such as Temasek and Zomato, Shiprocket has evolved from a shipping service provider into a full-stack e-commerce enablement platform serving direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
The company operates through two segments — Core Business and Emerging Business. Its core business comprises the domestic shipping platform and shipping apps, offering end-to-end shipping solutions in India, including multimodal transportation, AI-based logistics allocation, and order management and tracking tools.
The Emerging Business segment houses newer offerings such as cargo and fulfilment services, cross-border shipping, advertising and marketing solutions, capital solutions and hyperlocal deliveries, aimed at helping merchants expand and scale their operations.
Shiprocket follows an asset-light business model, with a scalable technology platform at the centre of its operations, supported by an extensive network of ecosystem partners.

Business
Incorporated in 2011, Shiprocket offers domestic and cross-border shipping services, marketing solutions, and merchant services to help them in business development. Its technology platform simplifies logistics, checkouts, payments, and fulfilment, enabling merchants to sell online and offline. The company has two main business lines: core and emerging. The shipping platform and related apps form the core business while the emerging operations include tools and platforms to facilitate heavy cargo movement, cross-border shipments, marketing ads and solutions. The emerging business is growing rapidly - its share in merchant addition improved to 21% in FY26 from 6.2% in FY24 while its share in revenue increased to 26.6% from 17.6%.
Financials
Revenue grew by 24% annually to ₹2,024 crore between FY24 and FY26. The annual revenue growth for the core and emerging businesses was 17% and 52.6%, respectively, during the period. The core business has been profitable with operating profit growing by 60% annually to ₹186.6 crore in the said period. The emerging business is yet to report a profit given its phase of rapid growth. The company reported a net loss of ₹79.2 crore in FY26. Total operating cash flow improved to ₹52.6 crore in FY26 from an outflow of ₹216 crore in FY24.
Valuation
Given the loss-making operations, price-sales (P/S) multiple will be more appropriate. The company demands a P/S multiple of 3.5 considering FY26 numbers and implied market cap. Unicommerce Esolutions, a profitable e-com enablement services provider, trades at a P/S of 4.7.

According to the Redseer Report, Shiprocket is the largest new-age, end-to-end horizontal e-commerce enablement platform in India, in terms of revenue from operations, for fiscal 2026. The company operates across two segments—Core Business and Emerging Business. Its core business includes domestic shipping and shipping applications, while its emerging businesses comprise cargo and fulfillment, cross-border shipping, advertising and marketing solutions, capital solutions, and hyperlocal deliveries. title: IPO-Bound Shiprocket Nets ₹727.4 Cr From Anchor Investors
content: Ahead of the commencement of the bidding for its public issue tomorrow (August 12), IPO-bound logistics major Shiprocket has raised ₹727.4 Cr from anchor investors. The startup allotted 7.5 Cr equity shares to anchor investors at a price of ₹97 per share, the upper band of its price spectrum. Of the total, over 5 Cr shares, or 66.8% of the total anchor round, were picked up by thirteen domestic mutual funds via a total of 31 schemes. The domestic mutual funds that anchored the round included HDFC Mutual Fund, Nippon Life, Kotak Mahindra, Mirae Asset, SBI Mutual Funds, among others. Besides, 53.4 Lakh equity shares, or 7.12% of the round, were picked up by insurance companies and pension funds including ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, Tata AIG Life Insurance, Axis Max Life Insurance, and Edelweiss Life Insurance. Other investors who participated in the round included Goldman Sachs, New York State Teachers Retirement System, PGIM, Societe Generale, Susquehanna Pacific, among others. With this, the Delhi NCR-based startup’s ₹1,617 Cr IPO will open for subscription tomorrow and subsequently close on August 14 (Friday). At the upper end of ₹92 to ₹97 price band, the public issue values Shiprocket at about ₹7,000 Cr. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹885.5 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to ₹732 Cr. To note, the startup cut the issue size by 30% compared to the ₹1,100 Cr fresh issue and the ₹1,242 Cr OFS proposed in its updated DRHP. Cofounders Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor, Akshay Ghulati and Vishesh Khurana will participate in the OFS. Goel and Kapoor will sell shares worth ₹61 Cr each, while Khurana will offload shares worth ₹20 Cr. Existing institutional investors Lightrock and Tribe Capital will also sell part of their holdings through the IPO. If the listing materialises, Shiprocket will become the third Indian logistics startup to list on the bourses, after Delhivery and Shadowfax. The startup became India's 106th unicorn in 2022, after raising $33.5 Mn at a valuation of $1.2 Bn. Overall, it has raised $420 Mn in capital from investors like Razorpay, PayPal Ventures, Info Edge Ventures, Temasek, among others. On the financial front, Shiprocket’s net loss widened over 6% to ₹79.2 Cr in FY26 from ₹74.5 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, its top line increased by 24% to ₹2,024 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹1,632 Cr in FY25.

title: Shiprocket IPO: A profitable core, a pricey bet
content:
Anand Kumar/AI-Generated Image
हिंदी में भी पढ़ें
Summary: Shiprocket's core shipping business is profitable, increasingly efficient and generating cash, but its newer businesses are still consuming those gains. At the IPO valuation, investors are being asked to pay for growth that these new bets have yet to prove.
Most of us shop online these days. Clothes, shoes, cosmetics, you name it. And once an order is packed and ready to dispatch, a notification pops up on your phone, usually from a logistics partner: "Your order is out for delivery!"
Shiprocket is one of the platforms powering that experience behind the scenes. The company opens its IPO tomorrow (August 12, 2026), with an issue size of approximately Rs 1,617 crore. The proceeds are expected to primarily fund the company's growth plans.
Here, we take a closer look at Shiprocket's financials and track record to help you decide whether the IPO is worth subscribing to.
About the company
When an independent merchant sells goods through their own website, social media or app, arranging delivery, warehousing and payment collection creates an operational hurdle. This is where Shiprocket comes in. It solves the issue by aggregating merchant volume onto a single digital platform. Sellers log in, compare rates across 42 active courier partners, print shipping labels, track parcels and handle cash-on-delivery collections through a unified dashboard.
The company earns its revenue primarily from a consumption-based model where merchants pay fees per shipment or service utilised. Revenue is divided into two primary segments. The core business, which includes domestic shipping and value-added shipping apps, brought in 73 per cent of total operating revenue in FY26. The emerging business, which includes cross-border logistics through ShiprocketX, quick commerce through Shiprocket Quick, marketing tools and capital solutions, generated the rest. Cargo and cross-border solutions are the biggest contributors within this newer segment.
What’s good
#1 Merchant acquisition is getting cheaper
Shiprocket attracts over 2.3 million unique monthly visitors, with nearly 43 per cent arriving organically without performance marketing. Once there, almost 97 per cent of merchants complete onboarding digitally without support staff. This self-serve model has steadily lowered customer acquisition costs, from over Rs 4,101 in FY24 to Rs 2,829 in FY26. The more sales and onboarding happen through software, the less Shiprocket needs to spend on acquiring each merchant.
#2 The core business has operating leverage
Core revenue grew 36.9 per cent over two years, while core staff costs rose just 8.3 per cent and other expenses 5.9 per cent. An extra parcel mainly requires more courier capacity, which Shiprocket buys and passes on, not more engineers, offices or support staff. The software is already built, so higher volumes come with relatively little additional overhead. Core adjusted EBITDA has consequently grown two and a half times since FY24.
#3 Cash flow has finally turned positive
Despite reporting net losses, Shiprocket's cash generation has improved sharply. Operating cash flow turned positive at Rs 52.6 crore in FY26, from an outflow of Rs 216 crore in FY24. The company is now generating operating cash, giving it a stronger base to fund its next phase of growth.
What’s bad
#1 New bets are eating into a profitable core
Shiprocket's domestic shipping business grew over 13 per cent in FY26 and generated Rs 187 crore in adjusted EBITDA. But management is pushing into cross-border, hyperlocal and other new businesses that are already consuming those gains. The emerging segment lost Rs 169 crore in adjusted EBITDA in FY26, extending losses since FY24. High fixed costs make matters worse, with employee costs alone exceeding 32 per cent of segment revenue.
#2 The middleman is exposed
Shiprocket depends entirely on third-party delivery fleets. It works with 42 active couriers, but five handled 84.5 per cent of shipment volumes in FY26. With no exclusive contracts, these partners can raise tariffs or impose surcharges, leaving Shiprocket with limited bargaining power. There is also a bigger threat: the couriers own the physical delivery network and could build their own merchant-facing platforms. If they bypass Shiprocket, its role as the middleman becomes far less valuable.
#3 Its most valuable merchants have stopped growing
Power merchants (sellers doing more than 100 transactions per month) rose from 9,020 to 10,005 to just 10,090 over the last three years. Growth slowed to just under one per cent. Yet this tiny group, only 4.7 per cent of merchants, generates nearly 89 per cent of FY26 revenue at Rs 17.8 lakh per merchant. In other words, almost nine-tenths of revenue depends on a group that added just 85 merchants last year.
Shiprocket IPO Details
Post-IPO
Financial history
Key ratios
Operating metrics
What the numbers tell us
Run your eye down Shiprocket's prospectus and the conclusion seems obvious. The company has lost money in each of the last three years and posted an operating loss of Rs 103 crore on Rs 2,024 crore of revenue in FY26. On the surface, this looks like a business that has yet to find its economics.
Look underneath, and the picture changes. Shiprocket's core shipping business is already profitable, gets more efficient as it scales and is now generating cash. The problem is that those profits are being used to fund businesses that have yet to prove their economics. So the real question is not whether Shiprocket can make money. It is whether the profits from a business that works can justify the cost of building businesses that don't, yet.
What the price is actually asking you to believe
Price-to-earnings is of little use because Shiprocket is still loss-making. Price-to-revenue is the cleaner measure. At the post-IPO market cap, Shiprocket will trade at about 3.5 times FY26 revenue. Unicommerce, the only listed Indian peer cited in the prospectus, trades at 4.6 times. Unicommerce is much smaller but already profitable, while Shiprocket is growing faster and has greater scale. The lower multiple therefore looks reasonable at first glance, but the comparison changes once you look at the quality of that revenue.
Unicommerce primarily sells software and keeps most of what it bills. Shiprocket bills merchants for the entire shipment and then pays the courier. After courier payments, only about 26 paise of every rupee billed remains with Shiprocket before its other costs. On that retained revenue, its valuation works out to roughly 14 times, versus 4.7 times for Unicommerce. This is not a like-for-like valuation measure, but it shows why the headline revenue multiple can make Shiprocket look cheaper than it really is.
The IPO gives Shiprocket roughly Rs 675 crore of fresh capital after debt repayment. The question is whether that money creates value or simply funds more losses. The core business has proved its economics. At this price, the rest still has to prove its worth.

title: Shiprocket bets IPO proceeds on AI as it expands beyond core shipping biz
content:
Shiprocket bets IPO proceeds on AI as it expands beyond core shipping biz
Shiprocket plans to invest much of its IPO proceeds in AI and emerging businesses as it seeks to offer merchants technology spanning advertising, freight and commerce
Listen to This Article
	Shiprocket plans to funnel much of the proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO) into artificial intelligence (AI), betting the technology can turn the Indian e-commerce (ecom) enablement platform into a broader operating system for merchants.
 
	The company wants to let merchants run their businesses through conversational commands rather than multiple software tabs, while using AI internally to cut time spent on data collection and manual tasks.
 
	“We are basically trying to bring the AI experience to the merchant,” Saahil Goel, managing director and chief executive officer (MD & CEO) of Shiprocket, told Business Standard.
 
	Most of the IPO capital, after debt repayment, will go towards the company's faster-growing emerging business, including technology and sales & marketing, he said. The emerging business has grown to ₹538.7 crore in revenue for financial year 2025-26 (FY26), compared with roughly ₹1,485.4 crore for core business for the same period. The emerging business is growing at about 65 per cent, Goel said.
 
	Shiprocket will open its IPO on August 12, pricing shares at ₹92 to ₹97 apiece. The issue size has been cut about 30 per cent to ₹1,617 crore, with the fresh issue reduced to ₹885 crore and the offer for sale (OFS) to ₹732 crore. At the upper end of the price band, Shiprocket would be valued at ₹7,056 crore, a roughly 30 per cent decline from its ₹10,000 crore valuation when it last raised capital in December 2024.
Also Read
	Lightrock, the largest-selling shareholder, is offloading shares worth ₹272 crore but is expected to realise only about 0.72 times its investment. McKinsey, through AFOS, and Moore Strategic Ventures are also selling below cost, with estimated returns of 0.59 times and 0.67 times, respectively. Cofounders Goel, Gautam Kapoor, and Vishesh Khurana are also selling stakes, about ₹61 crore each for Goel and Kapoor, and ₹20 crore for Khurana. Bertelsmann India Investments, Shiprocket's largest shareholder, has withdrawn from the OFS, and Eternal, formerly Zomato, and Temasek are also not selling.
	 But industry sources that most of big investors are not exiting and that shows trust in the business.
 
	 Goel said Lightrock India is the only fund exiting, a sign, he said, that long-term shareholders believe significant value remains to be unlocked. The gap in investor returns reflects how private and public markets price differently, he said. With 2.14 lakh merchants on the platform and the business growing about 24-25 per cent, more than 80 per cent of the founders' wealth remains tied up in the company.
 
	Internally, AI would cut the time employees spend on data collection and mechanical tasks, Goel said, freeing them for decision-making. Shiprocket sees its next opportunity in roughly 20 million “glass door merchants” among India's 60 million retail MSMEs and 40 million kiranas. Its newer products, including advertising, freight and quick commerce (qcom), are gaining traction across merchant categories.
	Goel said the investments extend Shiprocket's reach without diluting its core focus, calling the company's scale hard to replicate. “It cannot be done with money,” he said. Built over 14 years, Shiprocket now handles about 4-5 per cent of India's ecom market, and data from over 150 million Indian consumers and more than 700 million deliveries gives it an edge in understanding fraud risk and courier performance.
 
	Shiprocket had signed a joint venture (JV) with Ultrasafe AI in September 2025 to build foundational AI model, but the agreement lapsed. Goel said India needs its own AI stack, partly because foreign models are designed for workers costing $30,000-50,000 a year in developed markets, versus roughly ₹2-4 lakh in India. As open-source models advanced, Shiprocket shifted focus to applied AI, and has since built its own voice model, trained on its own call-centre data, which is already used internally and will be offered to merchants.
	The company’s global strategy is to help Indian small businesses sell overseas rather than launching abroad, since artisanal businesses often sell to exporters at 5-10 per cent margins while intermediaries capture more value internationally. It has built cross-border lanes linking foreign postal networks with Customs and freight facilities in India, enabling 7-10-day deliveries. Goel said the company has no plans to launch abroad, since India's digital retail penetration is only about 8 per cent.
 
	Shiprocket made several acquisitions in 2021-22. The last three — Pickrr, Shiprocket Omuni, and Swiftly — led to real goodwill writedowns. Goel said the acquisition strategy has since evolved, and that omnichannel and martech, both acquired, are now among its fastest-growing segments.
	Going public has instilled greater discipline and governance in Shiprocket rather than stifling innovation, Goel said. This comes as the company scales towards ₹2,000 crore in revenue, with its core business being the clear market leader, he added.
 
	Shiprocket reported a 24 per cent Y-o-Y increase in operating revenue to ₹2,024 crore in FY26 from ₹1,632 crore in FY25, according to its RHP (red herring prospectus) financial statements. Its consolidated net loss widened to ₹79.25 crore in FY26 from ₹74.45 crore in FY25, a rise of about 6.5-7 per cent Y-o-Y.
 
	Operating cash flow was positive at more than ₹50 crore in FY26, versus about ₹1.9 crore the previous year, Goel said. The core business generated ₹186 crore in cash Ebitda (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) and has been profitable since FY22. Its Ebitda margin has risen from about 6 per cent to 12 per cent and cash generation has increased to more than ₹180 crore from about ₹70 crore three years earlier. The net loss largely reflects planned investment in the emerging business, not cash burn, with contribution margins turning positive as products scale, he said. Adjusted Ebitda was about ₹17 crore in FY26 after accounting for ESOP (employee stock option plan) costs.
	With just 2.14 lakh of India's roughly 60 million businesses digitised on its platform, Goel said Shiprocket has significant room to grow without external funding. Its broader mission, he said, is to digitise India's merchants, giving every shopkeeper, retailer and kirana access to digital infrastructure for payments, advertising, shipping, and deliveries.

title: Shiprocket IPO: Ecommerce Enabler’s Public Issue Set To Open This Week - Should You Apply
content:
Summary of this article
- Shiprocket's public issue opens for subscription on August 12.
- The IPO price band is Rs 92 to Rs 97.
- Investors must assess the company's financial losses before applying.
The initial public offering (IPO) of ecommerce enabler Shiprocket is expected to open for subscription on August 12. The company filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) on August 5, 2026.
Notably, the public issue will be conducted as a 100 per cent book built offer. The issue is a combination of a fresh issue and an offer for sale. The bidding window is scheduled to close on August 14.
Ahead of the opening of the bidding window, here is a detailed look at the details of the public issue and the company's business that investors should know before the public issue opens for subscription.
Shiprocket IPO: Offer Size and Selling Shareholders
Shiprocket’s IPO comprises a fresh issue aggregating up to Rs 885.50 crore. The public issue also includes an offer for sale aggregating up to Rs 731.98 crore by selling shareholders. Shiprocket’s total offer size aggregates up to Rs 1,617.48 crore. The company is professionally managed and does not have an identifiable promoter. Pre-issue, the public shareholding is 100 per cent and the post-issue shareholding will not decrease.
Shiprocket IPO: Price Band and Lot Size
Shiprocket has set the price band for its public issue at Rs 92 to Rs 97 per share. Retail investors can apply by placing bids for a minimum of 154 shares, which amounts to a minimum investment of Rs 14,938.
Small non-institutional investors (sHNI) can bid for the issue by applying for a minimum of 14 lots or 2,156 shares, aggregating to Rs 2,09,132, and for the big non-institutional investor (bHNI) category, the minimum amount will be 67 lots or 10,318 shares, amounting to
Rs 10,00,846.
Shiprocket IPO: GMP
The current trends in the Grey Market Premium (GMP) for Shiprocket’s shares indicates a premium of Rs 16 above the upper end of the price band. Based on the upper price band of Rs 97, the estimated listing price is Rs 113, indicating an expected listing gain of 16.49 per cent per share.
Shiprocket IPO: Key Financials
In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, Shiprocket's total revenue from operations stood at Rs 2,077.42 crore, increasing by 24.03 per cent compared to Rs 1,674.82 crore in the preceding fiscal. The company posted a restated loss of Rs 79.25 crore in the same period compared to a restated loss of Rs 74.45 crore in the preceding fiscal. The net worth of the ecommerce enabler grew by 2 per cent to Rs 1524.29 crore compared to Rs 1491.23 crore in the preceding fiscal.
Shiprocket: Business Model
Shiprocket is a technology-enabled logistics platform providing shipping, fulfillment, warehousing, and order management solutions. The company's core business is its domestic shipping platform which provides merchants with access to logistics partners to deliver goods to end consumers within India, and Shipping Apps. Its Emerging Business includes cross-border services, checkout platforms, marketing solutions, and hyperlocal deliveries. The domestic shipping platform contributed to 73.38 per cent of the company’s total Revenue from Operations in FY26.
Shiprocket: Competitors
Shiprocket competes in various aspects of its business with other aggregators that streamline services for merchants, large marketplaces, dedicated third-party logistics providers, and other courier companies enhancing their digital capabilities to offer self-serve platforms. The company has only one listed peer named Unicommerce Esolutions.
Shiprocket IPO: Should You Apply?
Ahead of the upcoming public issue, investors should assess the risks and strengths related to the company's business model before applying.
Shiprocket IPO: Key Risks
- Shiprocket has incurred losses in the last two fiscals, Inability to generate adequate revenue growth can make the company incur losses again.
- Shiptocket’s results of operations are impacted by the operational results and business decisions of its merchants.
- The company mentioned in the RHP that it does not have exclusive arrangements with logistics partners, who may prioritise competitors or expand their own offerings to compete.
Shiprocket IPO: Key Strengths
- Shiprocket has a diversified merchant base, serving 2,14,769 active Merchants in FY26.
- The platform processes a high volume of transactions and consumer data and has integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to enhance product features and operational functions.
- The company offers an end-to-end ecosystem covering shipping, payments, checkout, and marketing by relying on various third-party vendors.
Shiprocket IPO: Objective
The company intends to use the fresh issue proceeds for investment in the growth of Shiprocket's platforms such as marketing initiatives and technology infrastructure related to its emerging and core businesses. The proceeds will also be used for the repayment or prepayment, in full or in part, of certain borrowings, funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions, and for general corporate purposes.

title: Shiprocket IPO: Who Is Cashing In, Where ₹885 Cr Will Go And What Could Go Wrong?
content:
- Shiprocket’s ₹1,617.48 crore IPO will open for subscription on August 12 at a price band of ₹92–97 per share
- Its founders could see return multiples of over 346x, while some institutional investors may face losses at ₹97
- Shiprocket remains loss-making and heavily dependent on vendors despite 24% revenue growth in FY26
Logistics-tech start-up Shiprocket is set to open its ₹1,617.5 crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on August 12, marking its entry into the public markets. The IPO will open for subscription on August 12.
The company had filed its draft IPO papers with Sebi through the confidential pre-filing route in May and subsequently received the regulator's approval in November to launch the public issue.
Shiprocket will command a post-issue market valuation of about ₹7,058 crore, while at the lower end, the valuation has been pegged at ₹6,739 crore.
Shiprocket runs a technology-driven platform that helps MSMEs and large retailers in India manage their e-commerce operations, covering logistics, checkout, payments, financing, order fulfilment and cross-border commerce.
What's On Offer?
The platform has fixed a price band of ₹92-97 per share for its ₹1,617.5 crore IPO. Investors can bid for a minimum of 154 equity shares and in multiples thereof, starting August 12. The initial share sale will conclude on August 14, while the bidding for anchor investors will open for a day on August 11.
Advertisement
The basis of allotment is likely to be finalised on August 17, with Shiprocket shares scheduled to debut on the NSE and BSE on August 19.
It has reduced its IPO size by 31% to ₹1,617.48 crore from the proposed ₹2,342.35 crore in its updated draft red herring prospectus. The fresh issue has been reduced from ₹1,100 crore to ₹885.5 crore, while the OFS has been cut from ₹1,242.35 crore to ₹731.98 crore.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 9.13 crore equity shares, while existing shareholders will offload 7.55 crore shares through the OFS.
As much as 75% of the offer has been reserved for Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs), 15% for Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) and the remaining 10% for retail investors.
Advertisement
Shiprocket has also reserved shares worth up to ₹1 crore for eligible employees, who may be offered the shares at a discount to the final issue price. Bertelsmann is the company’s largest shareholder with a 21.32% stake, followed by Tribe Capital at 14.14%, Eternal at 6.85%, KDT Venture Holdings at 5.49% and Temasek-backed MacRitchie Investments at 5.29%.
Four investment banks will oversee the share sale. Axis Capital, BofA Securities India, JM Financial and Kotak Mahindra Capital have been appointed as the book running lead managers.
Who’s Gaining And Who’s Losing?
Shiprocket IPO can deliver multi-fold gains to its early backers, while some later stage investors could face potential losses at the upper price band of ₹97 per share.
Among the founders, Vishesh Khurana stands to gain the most on a multiple basis. With a weighted average acquisition cost (WACA) of just ₹0.27 per share, his ₹20 crore OFS translates into a 359.3x return multiple at ₹97. This implies a potential gain of nearly ₹19.9 crore.
Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel, whose WACA stands at ₹0.28 per share, are each selling shares worth ₹61 crore. At ₹97, the two could see a 346.4x return multiple, translating into potential gains of around ₹60.8 crore each.
Institutional investors like 500 Startups III are also on the same side of the ledger. It could see a 77.6x return multiple on its ₹16.3 crore OFS, implying a potential gain of about ₹16.1 crore. Tribe Capital III, with a WACA of ₹12.66, could see a 7.7x multiple on its ₹120 crore OFS, translating into a potential gain of around ₹104.3 crore.
MCP3 SPV and Agility International Investment are also in the money, with return multiples of 2.1x and 2.6x, respectively, at ₹97.
But LR India Fund I and Moore Strategic Ventures could take a hit. Their WACAs of ₹133.94 and ₹143.82, respectively, are above Shiprocket’s ₹97 upper price band. Their shares would, therefore, fetch only 0.72x and 0.67x their acquisition costs, implying potential losses of around ₹103.6 crore and ₹24.8 crore, respectively.
It is pertinent to note that these gains and losses are indicative calculations based on the ₹97 upper price band and the maximum OFS value disclosed in Shiprocket’s RHP. The actual returns will depend on the final issue price and other applicable costs.
Where Will Shiprocket Deploy IPO Funds?
With its public market debut, Shiprocket is looking to scale its technology capabilities, expand its operations and fuel its next phase of growth as India’s e-commerce and digital commerce infrastructure market expands.
Of the fresh issue proceeds, ₹294 crore has been earmarked for marketing and brand-building, while ₹211 crore will go towards strengthening technology infrastructure and capabilities across its core and emerging businesses.
The company plans to use another ₹210 crore to repay or prepay certain borrowings, including accrued interest. In total, these payments account for over 65% of the fresh IPO proceeds.
The remaining, up to 35% of the proceeds, will be available for potential acquisitions and other inorganic growth opportunities, as well as general corporate purposes. This growth investment will be deployed between FY27 and FY29.
What Investors Should Know Before Bidding?
Shiprocket’s losses have narrowed sharply from FY24 levels, but the company is yet to turn profitable. Its net loss stood at ₹79.2 crore in FY26, compared with ₹74.4 crore in FY25, and was significantly lower than the ₹595.1 crore loss reported in FY24.
At the same time, growth has remained healthy. Revenue from operations rose 24% year-on-year to ₹2,024.1 crore in FY26, following a similar 24% increase in FY25. The key challenge now is to convert this growth into sustained profitability, particularly as the company continues to invest in its merchant base, technology, AI and newer businesses.
The start-up also remains heavily reliant on third-party vendors. Merchant solution costs accounted for 69.39% of its total expenses in FY26, while its top 10 vendors contributed 55.24%. The company does not have exclusive arrangements with logistics partners, leaving it exposed to potential cost increases, service disruptions and the risk of partners prioritising competitors.
Competition from e-commerce marketplaces, aggregators and logistics companies could further pressure margins, while scaling its relatively nascent cross-border business brings additional execution risks.
Its legal disclosures also flag four criminal cases against the company involving ₹5.39 crore, alongside two criminal and seven tax proceedings. Its subsidiaries face one criminal and three tax proceedings involving ₹2.34 crore.
Separately, a 2022 criminal case names co-founders Saahil Goel and Gautam Kapoor, director Arjun Sethi and CFO Kumar Tanmay, with allegations including cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery and conspiracy. The matter remains pending.
With the IPO, the focus will now be on whether Shiprocket can sustain its strong revenue growth while moving towards profitability.

Shiprocket has demonstrated strong revenue growth, though it continues to report net losses at the consolidated level. However, the loss trajectory has improved significantly from ₹595.18 Crore in FY2024 to ₹79.25 Crore in FY2026. The Core Business has been profitable since Fiscal 2022.
Operating cash flows turned positive in FY2025 (₹1.90 Crore) and improved to ₹52.64 Crore in FY2026, compared to negative ₹215.99 Crore in FY2024.
Risk Factors
Investors should consider the following material risks highlighted in the DRHP:
- Operating Losses: The company reported restated losses of ₹792.45 million in FY2026. There is no assurance of achieving consolidated profitability.
- Goodwill Impairment Risk: Goodwill represents 36.54% of total assets as of March 31, 2026. Significant impairment losses were recorded in FY2024 (₹1,767.42 million in goodwill).
- Partner Dependency: The company relies on 42 active courier partners with no exclusive arrangements. Top 5 partners handle 84.50% of total shipment volumes.
- Vendor Concentration: Top 10 vendors contribute 55.24% of total expenses, creating dependency risks.
- Legal Proceedings: Various legal proceedings involving aggregate amounts of ₹129.12 million are pending.
Valuation & Peer Comparison
As the price band and issue size are not yet disclosed, traditional valuation metrics like P/E ratio are not applicable due to the company's loss-making status. Valuation will likely be assessed based on revenue multiples (P/Sales) given the high-growth nature of the business. Peer comparison data is not available in the provided DRHP excerpt.
Bottom Line
Shiprocket presents a compelling case as a market leader in India's D2C enablement space with strong revenue growth (~24% YoY) and improving cash flows. However, investors must weigh these positives against ongoing consolidated losses, significant goodwill on the balance sheet, and dependencies on non-exclusive logistics partners. The IPO opens on 12-Aug-2026; investors should wait for the price band disclosure to assess valuation comfort levels.

title: Shiprocket IPO decoded: Smaller issue, bumper exits, key risks and the road ahead
content:
Shiprocket is heading to the public markets with a Rs 1,617.48-crore IPO, but with a smaller ask than it had initially planned. The logistics-tech company has cut the issue size by 31% from the Rs 2,342.35 crore proposed in its updated DRHP, trimming both the fresh issue and the investor sell-down.
The IPO comprises a Rs 885.5-crore fresh issue and a Rs 731.98-crore offer for sale (OFS). The fresh issue has been reduced from Rs 1,100 crore, while the OFS has been cut from Rs 1,242.35 crore. The price band is set at Rs 92-97 a share.
Axis Capital, BofA Securities India, JM Financial and Kotak Mahindra Capital are the book running lead managers to the issue.
For Shiprocket, the IPO brings fresh capital to fund its next phase of growth, while allowing some of its earliest backers to cash out. For some investors, the IPO could be a very lucrative payday, while for others, it could mean taking a haircut on their original investment.
Founders, early backers eye bumper exits
Shiprocket’s IPO is setting up sharply different outcomes for its early backers. At the Rs 97 upper end, some investors are sitting on multi-fold returns, while others are selling below their acquisition cost.
Vishesh Khurana stands out, with a WACA of just Rs 0.27. His Rs 20-crore OFS translates to a 359x multiple, or nearly Rs 19.9 crore in gains.
Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel, with a WACA of Rs 0.28, are each selling shares worth up to Rs 61 crore. That works out to 346x their acquisition cost, or gains of roughly Rs 60.8 crore each.
Early investor 500 Startups III is looking at a 77.6x return, while Tribe Capital could make 7.7x, translating to gains of roughly Rs 104 crore on its Rs 120-crore OFS. MCP3 SPV and Agility International could make around 2.1x and 2.6x, respectively.
But LR India Fund I and Moore Strategic Ventures are on the other side of the ledger. Their WACAs of Rs 133.94 and Rs 143.82 are above the IPO's upper band, meaning their OFS blocks would fetch only 0.72x and 0.67x their acquisition costs, potential losses of around Rs 103.5 crore and Rs 24.8 crore, respectively.
The multiples are calculated by comparing the Rs 97 IPO price with each investor’s disclosed weighted average acquisition cost; gains are based on the maximum OFS value disclosed.
Growth gets the biggest slice, debt repayment follows
Shiprocket plans to put the bulk of its Rs 885.5-crore fresh issue to work on growth and debt reduction.
The company has earmarked Rs 365.6 crore for expanding its platforms, including Rs 205.8 crore for marketing and Rs 159.8 crore for technology infrastructure and capabilities. Another Rs 210 crore will go towards repaying or prepaying borrowings.
Together, these account for about 65% of the fresh proceeds. The remaining up to 35% can be used for unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes, leaving room for Shiprocket to pursue inorganic growth.
The growth investments will be deployed over FY27-FY29, while the debt repayment is planned entirely for FY27.
Losses, vendor dependence cloud the picture
Shiprocket’s biggest challenge remains turning growth into sustainable profits. The company says continued investments in its merchant base, products, AI and emerging businesses could keep it under pressure.
The business is also heavily dependent on third-party partners. Merchant solution costs accounted for 69.39% of total expenses in FY26, while its top 10 vendors contributed 55.24%. With no exclusive arrangements with logistics partners, Shiprocket is exposed to higher costs, service disruptions and partners prioritising competitors.
Competition from marketplaces, aggregators and logistics providers, along with the risks of scaling its nascent cross-border business, add to the pressure. Its legal disclosures show four criminal cases against the company involving Rs 5.39 crore, besides two criminal and seven tax proceedings. Its subsidiaries face another one criminal and three tax proceedings involving Rs 2.34 crore.
Separately, a 2022 criminal case names co-founders Saahil Goel and Gautam Kapoor, director Arjun Sethi and CFO Kumar Tanmay, with allegations including cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery and conspiracy. The case remains pending.
Losses narrow sharply, but profits remain elusive
Shiprocket remains loss-making despite a sharp improvement in its bottom line over the past two years. Its net loss stood at Rs 79.2 crore in FY26, marginally higher than the Rs 74.4 crore loss in FY25 but sharply lower than the Rs 595.1 crore loss recorded in FY24.
The company’s topline continued to grow at a healthy pace, with revenue from operations rising 24% year-on-year to Rs 2,024.1 crore in FY26, following an identical 24% growth in FY25.
For Shiprocket, the challenge now is turning that growth into sustainable profitability. The IPO will put that equation under sharper scrutiny as the company uses fresh capital to fund growth, strengthen its technology and expand into newer businesses.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14, with the anchor book opening on August 11.

title: Shiprocket IPO: Why This ₹1,617.5 Crore Issue Is Different from Recent Startup Listings
content:
E-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket will open its ₹1,617.5-crore initial public offering on August 12, with the price band fixed at ₹92 to ₹97 per equity share. At the upper end of the band, the issue values the company at up to ₹7,056 crore.
Issue Structure and Key Dates
The IPO comprises a fresh issue worth up to ₹885.5 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth up to ₹731.9 crore by existing shareholders. Bids can be made for a minimum of 154 equity shares and in multiples thereof, translating to a minimum retail investment of ₹14,168 at the lower band and ₹14,938 at the upper band.
Source: Company RHP; BSE/NSE filings
Axis Capital, BofA Securities India, JM Financial and Kotak Mahindra Capital are the book-running lead managers, with KFin Technologies as registrar. Face value of the shares is ₹10 apiece.
Reservation and Employee Quota
At least 75% of the net offer is reserved for qualified institutional buyers, of which up to 60% may be allocated to anchor investors ahead of the issue. Non-institutional investors get 15% and retail individual investors get 10%, a notably smaller retail carve-out than the 35% typical of many mainboard issues. The IPO also includes an employee reservation worth up to ₹1 crore, with eligible employees eligible for a discount of up to ₹9 a share.

Selling Shareholders in the OFS
Lightrock is the largest selling shareholder, offloading shares worth ₹272 crore, but is expected to realise only about 0.72 times its original investment on the stake sold, per the offer documents. McKinsey (through AFOS) and Moore Strategic Partners are also selling below cost, at estimated returns of 0.59 times and 0.67 times respectively. Tribe Capital and Agility International Investment are among the other institutional sellers.
Co-founders Saahil Goel and Gautam Kapoor are each offloading shares worth about ₹61 crore, while co-founder Vishesh Khurana is selling shares worth ₹20 crore.
Bertelsmann India Investments, Shiprocket’s largest shareholder with a 21.3% stake, has withdrawn from the OFS after being included in the draft prospectus. Eternal (formerly Zomato), which holds a 6.85% stake, and Temasek are not selling shares in this issue.
Use of IPO Proceeds
The company plans to deploy fresh-issue proceeds toward marketing and technology investment across its core and emerging businesses, repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings, potential acquisitions, and general corporate purposes.

Financial Snapshot: FY24-FY26
Source: Company RHP, restated consolidated financials
Revenue growth held steady at roughly 24% year-on-year through FY26. However, net loss widened by about 6.8% to ₹79.25 crore in FY26 from ₹74.45 crore in FY25 — a reversal after the sharp 88% narrowing seen the previous year. EBITDA loss improved marginally, staying near breakeven levels.

About Shiprocket
Shiprocket’s parent entity, Bigfoot Retail Solutions, was incorporated in 2011; the Shiprocket platform itself was launched in 2017 by co-founders Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor and Vishesh Khurana as a standalone logistics aggregator. It has since expanded into a full-stack e-commerce enablement platform covering shipping, fulfilment, payments, cross-border trade and omnichannel commerce for MSMEs, D2C brands and large retailers, integrating with courier partners including Delhivery, FedEx, Aramex, Xpressbees, DTDC and Shadowfax.
Per the company’s RHP, Shiprocket served 214,769 active merchants in FY26, reaching more than 155 million end consumers across over 19,000 pin codes. According to a company-commissioned Redseer report cited in the offer documents, Shiprocket was India’s largest new-age, horizontal e-commerce enablement platform by revenue from operations in FY25. The company has no identifiable promoter and is professionally managed, with Chetan Kumar Mathur as Chairman and Saahil Goel as Managing Director and CEO.
Valuation Context
At the upper price band, Shiprocket’s ₹7,056-crore valuation marks a roughly 30% cut from the nearly ₹10,000-crore valuation it commanded in its last private funding round in December 2024. The issue size itself was also trimmed by close to 31% from the ₹2,342.3 crore proposed in the company’s updated draft prospectus filed in December 2025. As of this report, grey-market activity had not picked up, with trackers showing no meaningful premium ahead of the bid opening.

title: IPO-Bound Shiprocket FY26 Loss Widened 7% YoY To ₹79 Cr
content: In the run up to go public, logistics unicorn Shiprocket’s consolidated loss for the fiscal year FY26 increased by around 7% YoY to ₹79.2 Cr from ₹74.4 Cr in the previous fiscal year, as per the financial disclosures in its red herring prospectus (RHP). Operating revenue grew 24% to ₹2,024.1 Cr in the fiscal compared to ₹1,632 Cr in the previous year. Combined with other income of ₹53.3 Cr, the startup’s total income amounted to ₹2,077.4 Cr. Shiprocket also reported a loss of ₹3.3 Cr in exceptional items, and no tax expenses. Including items under “other comprehensive income/loss”, its total comprehensive loss for FY26 came to ₹79.3 Cr. The firm’s EBITDA loss for the fiscal decreased 3% to ₹16.6 Cr from ₹17.2 Cr EBITDA loss in FY25. Founded in 2017 by Gautam Kapoor, Saahil Goel, Vishesh Khurana and Akshay Ghulati, Shiprocket is a logistics aggregator for online sellers, partnering with third-party delivery services such as Delhivery, FedEx, Aramex, Xpressbees, DTDC and Shadowfax. It has also expanded into ecommerce enablement, providing brands with services such as cross-border shipping, payments, marketing tools, omnichannel commerce and merchant credit. The company also launched an on-demand hyperlocal delivery service in India, Shiprocket Quick, that allows businesses and individuals to send deliveries within a city. The startup, which has raised about $400 Mn in equity funding till date, joined the unicorn club in 2022, after raising $33.5 Mn in a round led by Lightrock India. Its other investors include Tribe Capital, March Capital, and Zomato’s parent company Eternal. Shiprocket is aiming for a valuation of around ₹7,000 Cr (about $736 Mn) in its IPO. The offer is set to open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14. It plans to raise up to ₹885.5 Cr via the fresh issue component of its IPO. Meanwhile, investors will cash in on shares worth up to ₹732 Cr via the offer for sale (OFS) component. The company intends to use a large chunk of the IPO proceeds, INR 365.6 Cr, to bolster marketing and IT infra for its core and emerging businesses. Besides, a comparatively smaller portion, INR 210 Cr, has been earmarked to repay or prepay certain borrowings availed by the company. On the other hand, Lightrock will be the biggest seller in the OFS component, offloading shares worth about ₹272 Cr. Investors like 500 Global, Agility International Investment, as well as the cofounders Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel will also paring stake in the company. Khuarana, who took up the role of a strategic advisor in April 2025, will also be offloading shares worth ₹20 Cr via the IPO. Bertelsmann India Investments is the largest shareholder in the company with a 21.3% stake, but will not be paring its stake in the IPO. Where Did Shiprocket Spend? In FY26, Shiprocket’s total expenses increased by around 23% to ₹2,153.4 Cr from ₹1,749.3 Cr in the previous fiscal. Here’s how the logistics major spent: Cost of Merchant Solutions: Expenditures on ecosystem partners like cloud infrastructure providers, credit providers, payment gateways, were Shiprocket’s largest expense, surging 23% YoY to ₹1,494.1 Cr. Employee Benefits Expense: Shiprocket spent ₹379.5 Cr on employee benefits in FY26, 21% more compared to the previous fiscal year. Purchase of Traded Goods: It spent ₹21.8 Cr on purchasing traded goods in FY26, more than double of its expenses under this head in FY25. Finance Cost: The company’s finance costs climbed around 20% YoY to ₹26.4 Cr.

title: Shiprocket Limited IPO announced: ₹575.60 crore issue, what you need to know
content:

Shiprocket Limited files DRHP for ₹575.60 crore IPO opening 12-Aug-2026. FY26 revenue hit ₹2,024.14 crore with narrowed losses of ₹79.25 crore. Proceeds will fund marketing, tech, and debt repayment. Key risks include goodwill impairment and courier dependency.

The company intends to raise ₹575.60 crore through a fresh issue, marking its entry into the public markets. The IPO is scheduled to open on 12-Aug-2026 and close on 14-Aug-2026.
Company Overview
Founded in 2011 and headquartered in New Delhi, Shiprocket operates a merchant-first, API-led technology platform that simplifies logistics, checkout, payments, fulfilment, and cross-border trade for India's MSMEs and Large Retailers. According to a Redseer Report cited in the DRHP, Shiprocket is the largest new-age end-to-end horizontal e-commerce enablement platform in India by revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026.
The platform serves 214,769 Active Merchants in Fiscal 2026, with 96.73% of onboarding completed via self-serve mechanisms. It has processed over 730 million unique transactions since October 2016 and maintains a 100.00% platform uptime in 2026. The business model relies on consumption-based revenue, directly linking earnings to merchant sales volumes.
Offer Details
The IPO structure involves a fresh issue with no Offer for Sale (OFS) mentioned in the available data. The total identified use of proceeds amounts to ₹575.60 crore.
Key Dates:
- IPO Opening Date: 12-Aug-2026
- IPO Closing Date: 14-Aug-2026
- Listing Date: Not Available
- Price Band: Not Available
Objects of Issue: The proceeds will be allocated as follows:
- Marketing Initiatives: ₹205.80 crore for performance marketing, affiliate programs, and merchant incentives.
- Technology Infrastructure: ₹159.80 crore for cloud infrastructure, product personnel, and data intelligence capabilities.
- Debt Repayment: ₹210.00 crore for prepayment of borrowings from banks and financial institutions.
- General Corporate Purposes: Amount not specified, intended for inorganic growth and operational expenses.
Financial Highlights
Shiprocket reported a significant improvement in its financial trajectory over the last three years. Revenue from operations grew at a CAGR of approximately 24.06% from FY2024 to FY2026. While the company remains loss-making on a consolidated basis, losses have narrowed substantially from ₹595.18 crore in FY2024 to ₹79.25 crore in FY2026. Operating cash flow turned positive in FY2025 and improved to ₹52.64 crore in FY2026.

title: Shiprocket IPO To Open On August 12, Issue Size Cut To ₹1,617 Cr
content: Logistics major Shiprocket has filed the RHP to raise ₹1,617 Cr (about $170 Mn) via its IPO, a 30% reduction from the ₹2,342.3 Cr proposed in its updated DRHP. The issue will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14. The company has fixed a price band of ₹92-97 per equity share for the public issue, valuing the company at around ₹7,000 Cr (about $736 Mn). The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹885.5 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) aggregating up to ₹732 Cr. In comparison, the company's UDRHP had proposed a fresh issue of ₹1,100 Cr and an OFS of about ₹1,242 Cr. Cofounders Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor, and Vishesh Khurana will pare their stakes as part of the OFS. Goel and Kapoor will offload shares worth ₹61 Cr each, while Khurana will sell shares worth ₹20 Cr. Among institutional investors, PE firm Lightrock will be the biggest seller in the OFS, offloading shares worth about ₹272 Cr. Silicon Valley-based Tribe Capital plans to sell shares worth ₹120 Cr. Other investors participating in the OFS include March Capital, 500 Global, Agility Global and Moore Strategic Ventures. Notably, Bertelsmann India Investments and Arvind Ltd, which were part of the OFS in the UDRHP, are no longer selling shares. Bertelsmann India Investments is the largest shareholder in the company with a 21.3% stake. Other large shareholders not paring their stakes include Zomato’s parent company Eternal, which owns a 6.85% stake in Shiprocket as of the date of filing the RHP. The Gurugram-based startup plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to invest in technology infrastructure, marketing initiatives, potential acquisitions, debt repayment and other general corporate purposes. Founded in 2017 by Goel, Kapoor, Khurana and Akshay Ghulati, Shiprocket started as a logistics aggregation platform and has since expanded into a full-stack ecommerce enablement player, offering services across shipping, warehousing, checkout, payments, marketing and cross-border commerce. On the financial front, Shiprocket reported a 24% increase in its operating revenue to ₹2,024 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,632 Cr in the previous year. However, its net loss widened over 6% to ₹79.2 Cr during the fiscal from ₹74.5 Cr in FY25. Most of its income was generated through the sale of services, namely merchant solutions, which fetched Shiprocket ₹2,008.1 Cr in FY26, while around ₹16 Cr was earned from the sale of traded goods. Its expenses during the year stood at ₹2,153.4 Cr, up 23% YoY from ₹1,749.2 reported in FY25. Notably, a bulk of its expenses went toward the cost of merchant solutions, which rose 23% YoY to ₹1,494.1 Cr. Once listed, Shiprocket will join listed logistics and fulfilment players such as Shadowfax and Delhivery on the bourses. Its IPO comes at a time when new-age tech IPOs have regained momentum, even as several players like Zepto, Flipkart and PhonePe have their public issues on hold.

title: Shiprocket Rs 1,617-crore IPO to hit Dalal Street on August 12, cuts offer size

title: How to Apply for a Business Loan as a Startup in India? (2026)
content:
- A business loan for a startup can help cover early expenses like hiring, setting up, buying inventory, and handling day-to-day operations.
- The process usually involves picking the right scheme, putting together a business plan, checking if you qualify, getting your documents ready, and applying.
- Government schemes like Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, SISFS, Stand-Up India, CGSS, and CGTMSE support startups with funding.
- Look at options like crowdfunding, venture capital, angel investors, grants, and bootstrapping.
- Platforms like Shiprocket Capital offer quick, digital access to working capital.
A strong idea is a good starting point, but it is rarely enough to build a business. Most startups need financial backing to get off the ground and keep things running in the early stages.
Business loans for startups are usually taken to handle early expenses like hiring, setting up operations, managing day-to-day costs, or buying inventory. Without enough funds coming in, even good ideas can struggle to take off.
According to a Small Industries Development Bank of India report, the MSME sector faces a credit gap of around Rs 30 lakh crore. This shows how important it is for entrepreneurs to find reliable funding options.
This blog explains why startups need loans, how the application process works, which government schemes are available, and what other funding options you can consider.
Why Do Startups Require Loans?
Starting and running a business comes with a range of expenses, and most of them show up early. A business loan for startups helps manage some of the most common expenses, such as:
- To Cover Initial Setup Costs: Setting up a business usually involves spending on equipment, workspace, licences, product development, and basic technology.
- Hiring Skilled Employees: Bringing in the right people early on can make a big difference, but it also requires upfront investment.
- Managing Daily Expenses: Rent, utilities, supplier payments, and other running costs need to be handled even before revenue becomes stable.
- Investing in Technology: Most businesses today depend on digital tools and systems. These are not optional, and they often require proper funding.
- Supporting Growth Plans: As the business picks up, additional funds may be needed to expand operations, enter new markets, or increase production.
How to Apply for a Startup Loan in India?
The process of applying for a startup loan is fairly straightforward, but it does require some preparation, like:
- Choosing the Right Loan or Scheme: Start by looking at different options such as Mudra Yojana, Stand-Up India, Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, or loans from banks and NBFCs. Compare key factors like interest rates, repayment terms, and loan limits before deciding.
- Preparing a Business Plan: Lenders usually expect a clear plan that explains what your business does, who it targets, how it will earn, and how the loan will be repaid.
- Checking Eligibility: Each scheme or lender has its own criteria. It is better to review these in advance rather than applying blindly.
- Arranging Documents: Keep all required documents ready. This usually includes identity proof, address proof, business details, bank statements, and financial records.
- Submitting the Application: Once everything is in place, you can apply through a bank, NBFC, or an official portal.
- Verification and Approval: The lender reviews your profile, checks your credit history, and evaluates your plan. If approved, the loan is sanctioned and disbursed.
What are Some Government Schemes Providing Business Loans for Startups?
To make funding more accessible, the government has introduced several schemes that reduce risk for both lenders and borrowers. These include:
- Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY): Offers collateral-free loans up to Rs 10 lakh under three categories:
  - Shishu: up to Rs 50,000
  - Kishor: Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh
  - Tarun: Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh
  - Tarun Plus: Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh for those who have already repaid a Tarun loan
- Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS): Supports early-stage startups with funding for product development, testing, and market entry.
- Stand Up India Scheme: Provides loans ranging from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 2 crore for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs starting new businesses.
- Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS): Helps startups access loans by offering guarantees to lenders, reducing their risk.
- Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE): Allows businesses to get loans without collateral by covering a portion of the lender’s risk.
What are Some Alternatives to Business Loans for Startups?
Loans are not the only way to raise funds. Depending on your situation, you might consider these options:
- Crowdfunding: Raising small contributions from a large group of people online, often used for new product ideas.
- Angel Investors: Individuals who invest in early-stage businesses in exchange for equity and sometimes guidance.
- Bootstrapping: Using personal savings or business income to fund growth, which helps retain full ownership.
- Government Grants and Subsidies: Some programmes offer financial support that does not need to be repaid.
- Venture Capital: Investment from firms that back high-growth startups in exchange for equity.
Get Working Capital up to Rs 5 Crores with Shiprocket
Running an online business often requires extra funds for inventory, marketing, or expansion Shiprocket Capital provides access to working capital of up to Rs 5 crores through its financing partners.
Shiprocket follows a revenue-based financing model, which means you can raise funds without giving up equity. Some key points include:
- Funding is usually processed within a few days after application
- No equity dilution involved
- Repayments are flexible and linked to cash flow
- The entire process is handled online
Conclusion
Getting access to funds at the right time can make a real difference in how a startup grows. Whether it is for setting up, managing operations, or expanding, a startup business loan can help ease the pressure in the early stages.
It is worth taking the time to understand the different schemes and funding options available before making a decision. The right choice depends on your business needs, stage, and future plans.
If you are considering funding options, platforms like Shiprocket Capital can simplify the process with quicker approvals and a fully digital experience, making it easier to secure working capital when you need it.
